ASAD-NOTES:24:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:intro/r3.claim: The surah stresses each person's right to privacy.
ASAD-NOTES:24:intro/r3.anchor: stress each individual's right to privacy

STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r7.claim: The surah sets etiquette for visiting homes, interaction between unrelated men and women, dress and modesty, and privacy at home.
STUDYQURAN:24:intro/r7.anchor: various rules of etiquette, such as those governing the visiting one another’s homes (vv. 27–29, 61) and the proper comportment between men and women

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r2.claim: Verses 27–31 regulate visiting other Muslims' homes and seeing those inside, while explaining restrictions for women present there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p288/r2.anchor: they must abide by certain decorum so that the eyes are restrained from taking undue liberty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r8.claim: Verses 27–34 prevent social disorder that leads to lustful looks, accusations, and sexual misconduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r8.anchor: In these verses, directives are given to prevent disorder in the society that leads to lustful stares, accusations and moral misconduct.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r9.claim: The passage first restricts the pre-Islamic freedom to visit other people's homes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p316/r9.anchor: first of all certain restrictions are imposed on the freedom that existed in pre-Islamic jāhiliyyah society regarding visiting one another in houses.

NAHHAS:v3p131/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p131/r11.speaker: عكرمة
NAHHAS:v3p131/r11.claim: ʿIkrima explains the command as “until you seek permission”; linguistically it derives from ānastu al-shayʾ, “I used or perceived the thing.”
NAHHAS:v3p131/r11.anchor: قال عكرمة أي حتى تستأذنوا وحقيقته في اللغة تستعملوا مشتق من آنست الشيء

NAHHAS:v3p131/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p131/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p131/r12.claim: Seeking permission is better than entering without it because unannounced entry creates suspicion.
NAHHAS:v3p131/r12.anchor: ذلك خير لكم ) أي من الدخول بغير استئذان لما فيه من التهمة

NAHHAS:v3p131/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p131/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p131/r13.claim: “So that you may remember” means so that you become alert to what benefits you.
NAHHAS:v3p131/r13.anchor: لعلكم تذكرون ) أي تنتبهون على ما لكم فيه الصلاح

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r1.claim: Rāzī connects the rule to the preceding slander rulings: seclusion gave people an opening for accusations, so permission and greeting are required to prevent suspicion and harm.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r1.anchor: لأن أهل الإفك إنما وجدوا السبيل إلى بهتانهم من حيث اتفقت الخلوة

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r2.claim: The first question notes that istiʾnās ordinarily means sociability through companionship, apparently something that would follow entering and greeting; the Qur’an also uses it for lingering to converse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r2.anchor: الاستئناس عبارة عن الأنس الحاصل من جهة المجالسة

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr are reported to interpret the wording as “until you seek permission”; this account alleges the scribe erred.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ، إنما هو حتى تستأذنوا فأخطأ الكاتب

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r4.speaker: أبي
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r4.claim: Ubayy’s reading is given as “until you seek permission for yourselves.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي : حتى تستأذنوا لكم

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r5.claim: Greeting is better than the pre-Islamic greeting and than damūr, entry without permission; damūr is linked to destruction because its perpetrator has committed a grave offense.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r5.anchor: وهو الدخول بغير إذن واشتقاقه من الدمار

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r6.speaker: الحديث
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report says that the person whose eye precedes his request for permission has committed damūr, a serious breach.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r6.anchor: من سبقت عينه استئذانه فقد دمر

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r7.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that Ibn Abbas meant a scribal error: it would impugn the multiply transmitted Qur’an and privilege a non-mass-transmitted reading, opening doubt about the whole text.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أن هذا القول من ابن عباس فيه نظر لأنه يقتضي الطعن في القرآن الذي نقل بالتواتر

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r8.speaker: الحسن البصري
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī proposes fronting and delaying: the intended order is to greet the household and then seek familiarity.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r8.anchor: الحسن البصري أنه قال إن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r9.speaker: عبدالله
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r9.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh puts greeting before asking permission.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r9.anchor: قراءة عبدالله : حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r10.claim: Rāzī calls the reordered construction weak because it departs from the apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r10.anchor: وهذا أيضا ضعيف لأنه خلاف الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r11.claim: On the apparent wording, one explanation is that permission and greeting reassure the household, whereas unpermitted entry unsettles and burdens them.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r11.anchor: حتى تستأنسوا بالإذن وذلك لأنهم إذا استأذنوا وسلموا أنس أهل البيت

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r12.claim: The preferred explanation takes istiʾnās as seeking information or finding out whether entry is wanted, from ānasa in the sense of seeing something manifest.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r12.anchor: تفسير الاستئناس بالاستعلام والاستكشاف استفعال من آنس الشيء إذا أبصره ظاهرا مكشوفا

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r13.claim: He cites “استأنس هل ترى أحدا” and “استأنست فلم أر أحدا” as idioms meaning to ascertain or investigate whether anyone is present.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r13.anchor: واستأنست فلم أر أحدا أي تعرفت واستعلمت

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r14.claim: When asked why greeting does not come first as in the Prophet’s formula “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”, Rāzī answers that a visitor may not know whether anyone is home; ask first, then greet face to face after permission.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r14.anchor: قلنا المستأذن ربما لا يعلم أن أحدا في المنزل فلا معنى لسلامه والحالة هذه

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r15.claim: A third explanation derives istiʾnās from ins: first establish whether a person is there, which necessarily precedes greeting.
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r15.anchor: من الإنس وهو أن يتعرف هل ثم إنسان

RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p170#2/r16.claim: A fourth answer says that even if familiarity follows greeting, the coordinating wāw does not require chronological order, so the order of mention need not dictate the order of action.

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying permission is sought three times: the first and second requests have the stated purposes, and at the third the household may admit or refuse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r1.anchor: روى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( الاستئذان )

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r2.speaker: جندب
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r2.claim: Jundub says he heard the Prophet instruct that a person who asks permission three times without being admitted should leave.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r2.anchor: عن جندب قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( إذا استأذن أحدكم ثلاثا

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recounts witnessing for Abū Mūsā: after Abū Mūsā left when ʿUmar failed to answer three requests, ʿUmar demanded proof of the Prophetic rule and Abū Saʿīd testified.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r3.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : ( كنت جالسا في مجلس من مجالس الأنصار

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r4.speaker: بعض الأخبار
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r4.claim: Another account says ʿUmar told Abū Mūsā that he did not suspect him but feared people might attribute statements falsely to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار أن عمر قال لأبي موسى

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r5.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r5.claim: Qatāda explains the three requests as letting occupants hear, giving them time to prepare, and allowing them to admit or refuse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة الاستئذان ثلاثة : الأولى يسمع الحي

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r6.claim: Rāzī treats three spaced requests as proper etiquette: the first may meet occupants at work, the second may encounter an impediment, and silence at the third signals a reason or reluctance, so the visitor should leave.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r6.anchor: وفي المرة الثانية ربما كان هناك ما يمنع

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r7.claim: He says the three requests should not be consecutive; time should separate each one from the next.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r7.anchor: يجب في الاستئذان ثلاثا ، أن لا يكون متصلا

RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r8.claim: Forceful knocking and shouting to the homeowner are forbidden because they cause distress and alarm; the Banū Asad incident and 49:4 warn against this conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172/r8.anchor: فذاك حرام لأنه يتضمن الإيذاء والإيحاش

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r1.claim: A report says Abū Saʿīd sought permission while facing the door; the Prophet told him not to ask permission while standing directly before it.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r1.anchor: روي أن أبا سعيد استأذن على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو مستقبل الباب

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r2.claim: Another report says the Prophet approached a household’s door from its right or left corner, greeted them, and did not face the door directly because houses then had no curtains.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r2.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا أتى باب قوم لم يستقبل الباب من تلقاء وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r3.claim: Although “until” might seem to permit entry after asking without receiving consent, Rāzī says the endpoint is actual reassurance, which arises only after permission is granted.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r3.anchor: أن الله تعالى جعل الغاية الاستئناس لا الاستئذان

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r4.claim: The purpose of permission is to prevent upsetting another by entering without consent; requesting permission alone cannot achieve that purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r4.anchor: أن الحكمة في الاستئذان أن لا يدخل الإنسان على غيره بغير إذنه فإن ذلك مما يسوءه

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r5.claim: Verse 28 explicitly forbids entry when no one is present until permission is given, showing that consent is also required by the first verse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r5.anchor: فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا فلا تدخلوها حتى يؤذن لكم

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a man’s messenger to another man counts as the man’s permission.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r6.anchor: روى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( رسول الرجل

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r7.claim: A second report from Abū Hurayra says a person invited to come with the messenger has permission and need not seek it again.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r7.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( إذا دعي أحدكم فجاء مع الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r8.claim: These reports show that permission is implicit in “until you seek familiarity” and that arriving with an invitation-bearing messenger requires no second request.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الخبر يدل على معنيين أحدهما : أن الإذن محذوف

RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r9.claim: Some jurists say that a person customarily allowed to enter does not need to seek permission anew.
RAZI-FULL:v23p172#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن من قد جرت العادة له بإباحة الدخول فهو غير محتاج إلى الاستئذان

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī rules that if a person peeping into someone’s home has his eye put out, the eye is forfeit and no compensation is due.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : لو فقئت عينه فهي هدر

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r2.speaker: سهل بن سعد
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r2.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports that a man peered into the Prophet’s chamber with a small comb; the Prophet said he would have stabbed the man’s eye and stressed that permission precedes looking.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r2.anchor: تمسك بما روى سهل بن سعد قال : ( اطلع رجل في حجرة

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that if a household gouges out the eye of someone peeking without permission, the eye is forfeit.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r3.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r4.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī rejects the report as contrary to legal analogy and consensus: if an unauthorized entrant’s eye is put out, the owner is liable to retaliation if intentional or compensation if accidental.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : هذا الخبر يرد

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r5.claim: Rāzī offers a possible construction of the report: a peeper looks at women’s private parts, persists after being stopped, and loses his eye during the ensuing resistance.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r5.anchor: فإن صح فمعناه : من اطلع في دار قوم ونظر إلى حرمهم ونسائهم فمونع فلم يمتنع

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r6.claim: For Rāzī, a mere look followed by gouging without prior warning or resistance is an injury for which the perpetrator is liable, under 5:45.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r6.anchor: فأما إذا لم يكن إلا النظر ولم يقع فيه ممانعة ولا نهي

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r7.claim: Rāzī says the appeal to 5:45 begs the question: the verse applies when the eye is not already forfeited, which is exactly what the dispute must establish.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r7.anchor: لأنا أجمعنا على أن هذا النص مشروط بما إذا لم تكن العين مستحقة

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r8.claim: Rāzī distinguishes entering from peeping: visible entry lets residents know and cover themselves, while a hidden look can expose what they would not permit others to see, warranting stronger deterrence.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r8.anchor: لأنه إذا دخل علم القوم دخوله عليهم فاحترزوا عنه وتستروا

RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r9.claim: Rāzī concludes that rejecting the Prophetic report on the basis of this argument is impermissible.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173/r9.anchor: وبالجملة فرد حديث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لهذا القدر من الكلام غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.claim: Rāzī reads the verse as accepting permission from anyone, including a child, woman, slave, or non-Muslim; permission need not meet testimony’s qualifications.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r1.anchor: ظاهر الآية يقتضي قبول الإذن مطلقا سواء كان الآذان صبيا أو امرأة أو عبدا أو ذميا فإنه لا يعتبر في هذا الإذن صفات الشهادة

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ b. Yasār reports that a man asked the Prophet whether he should seek permission to enter upon his sister; the Prophet said yes and asked whether he would want to see her naked.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار : ( أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أستأذن على أختي ؟ فقال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام نعم أتحب أن تراها عريانة )

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.speaker: حذيفة
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.claim: A man asked Ḥudhayfa whether to seek permission before entering upon his sister; Ḥudhayfa warned that without permission he might see something distressing.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r3.anchor: وسأل رجل حذيفة أستأذن على أختي ، فقال إن لم تستأذن عليها رأيت ما يسوؤك

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Ibn ʿAbbās answered yes when asked about seeking permission to enter upon and provide for a sister, citing 24:59, which does not distinguish relatives from strangers.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء سألت ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما استأذن على أختي ومن أنفق عليها ؟ قال نعم إن الله تعالى يقول

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r5.claim: Rāzī concludes that permission is required before entering upon maḥram relatives, though the matter is easier because some parts of their bodies may lawfully be seen.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r5.anchor: واعلم أن ترك الاستئذان على المحارم وإن كان غير جائز إلا أنه أيسر لجواز النظر إلى شعرها وصدرها وساقها

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r6.claim: If the ban on sudden entry protects someone who may be unclothed, it applies to everyone except wives and owned slave women.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r6.anchor: إن كان لأجل أن ذلك الغير ربما كان منكشف الأعضاء فهذا دخل فيه الكل إلا الزوجات وملك اليمين

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r7.claim: If the concern is interrupting private activity, permission is required before entering anyone’s space, including a wife’s or slave woman’s.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r7.anchor: وإن كان لأجل أنه ربما كان مشتغلا بأمر يكره إطلاع الغير عليه وجب أن يعم في الكل ، حتى لا يكون له أن يدخل على الزوجة والأمة إلا بإذن

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r8.claim: Rāzī says evidentiary exceptions remove the need for permission in emergencies such as fire, a thief’s attack, or a manifest wrong.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r8.anchor: إذا عرض أمر في دار من حريق أو هجوم سارق أو ظهور منكر فهل يجب الاستئذان ؟ الجواب : كل ذلك مستثنى بالدليل

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r9.claim: Salām is a commanded Muslim practice that gives security, is the greeting of Paradise’s people, brings affection, and removes rancor and spite.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r9.anchor: وأما السلام فهو من سنة المسلمين التي أمروا بها ، وأمان للقوم وهو تحية أهل الجنة ومجلبة للمودة وناف للحقد والضغينة

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet’s account: after Adam sneezed and praised God, God taught him to greet the angels and said this would be the greeting of Adam and his descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r11.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet listing six Muslim rights: greeting on meeting, answering an invitation, giving private counsel, responding to a sneeze, visiting the sick, and attending a funeral.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r11.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet urging people to spread salām among themselves if they want rancor removed from their hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v23p173#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عمر قال قال رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r1.speaker: رجل من الأنصار
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r1.claim: An Anṣārī man reported that a woman asked how to handle visitors who entered while she was privately undressed; the Prophet told her to send them back, and the verse was revealed.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r1.anchor: روي : عن عدي بن ثابت عن رجل من الأنصار قال : جاءت امرأة إلى رسول الله عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r2.claim: “Other than your houses” follows the customary case of living in one’s own property; tenants and borrowers also need permission before entering.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r2.anchor: وصف البيوت بمغايرة بيوتهم خارج مخرج العادة التي هي سكنى كل أحد في ملكه

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r3.claim: Istīʾnās here means seeking permission from whoever has authority to grant it.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r3.anchor: أي تستأذنوا ممن يملك الإذن من أصحابها.

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r4.claim: The word can mean inquiry and uncovering someone’s state, or becoming at ease after the fear that permission may be refused.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r4.anchor: من الاستئناس بمعنى الاستعلام من آنس الشيء إذا أبصره مكشوفا فعلم به

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r5.claim: The wording is metonymy: it names the ease that follows permission while intending permission itself.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r5.anchor: فيؤول المعنى إلى أن يؤذن لكم وهو من باب الكناية حيث ذكر الاستئناس اللازم وأريد الإذن الملزوم

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r6.claim: When asked what seeking familiarity means, the Prophet said to say tasbīḥ or takbīr and clear one’s throat to alert the household.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r6.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام في معنى الاستئناس حين سئل عنه فقال : "هو أن يتكلم الرجل بالتسبيحة والتكبيرة ويتنحنح يؤذن أهل البيت"

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r7.speaker: نصاب الاحتساب
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r7.claim: A cited legal manual permits a wife to enter the homes of her husband’s maḥram relatives without their permission; the author calls this an unusual ruling to verify.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r7.anchor: قال في "نصاب الاحتساب" : امرأة دخلت في بيت غير بغير إذن صاحبه هل يحتسب عليها؟ فالجواب

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة رحمه الله
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r8.claim: The cited ruling says a wife who steals from her husband’s maḥram relatives’ home is not subject to hand amputation according to Abū Ḥanīfa.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r8.anchor: ولهذا لو سرقت من بيت محارم زوجها لا قطع عليها عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله

BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r9.claim: In other cases, a woman is subject to the same enforcement of the permission rule as a man.
BURSEVI:v6p97#2/r9.anchor: وما في غير ذلك يحتسب عليها كما يحتسب على الرجل لقوله تعالى : {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا}

BURSEVI:v6p98/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r1.claim: Entering with permission is fine etiquette and a praiseworthy act that brings happiness in both worlds.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r1.anchor: فالدخول بالإذن من الآداب الجميلة والأفعال المرضية المستتبعة لسعادة الدارين

BURSEVI:v6p98/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r2.claim: One should say salām while seeking entry, ask three times, enter and greet again if permitted, and otherwise return.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r2.anchor: بأن يقول : السلام عليكم أدخل ثلاث مرات فإن أذن له دخل وسلم ثانيا وإلا رجع.

BURSEVI:v6p98/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r3.claim: Permission and greeting are better than entering suddenly, even into one’s mother’s home, since she might be unclothed.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r3.anchor: من أن تدخلوا بغتة ولو على الأم فإنها تحتمل أن تكون عريانة.

BURSEVI:v6p98/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r4.claim: The rule guides Muslims away from the pre-Islamic habit of greeting a strange household with “good morning” or “good evening” on entry.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r4.anchor: وفيه إرشاد إلى ترك تحية أهل الجاهلية حين الدخول فإن الرجل منهم كان إذا دخل بيتا غريبا صباحا.

BURSEVI:v6p98/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p98/r5.claim: Kāshifī advises announcing one’s arrival at home by speaking, calling out, or clearing the throat so residents can cover themselves and prepare.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وكفته اند كسي كه برعيال خود درمي آيد بايدكه بكلمة يا بآ وازيا بتنحنحى اعلام كند

BURSEVI:v6p98/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r6.claim: “So that you may remember” depends on an omitted clause: the command was given so people would remember, take heed, and act accordingly.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r6.anchor: متعلق بمضمر أي أمرتم به كي تذكروا وتتعظوا وتعلموا بموجبه.

BURSEVI:v6p98/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r7.claim: Salām is a Muslim sunnah and the greeting of Paradise; it produces affection and removes resentment and rancor.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r7.anchor: اعلم أن السلام من سنة المسلمين وهو تحية أهل الجنة ومجلبة للمودة وناف للحقد والضغينة

BURSEVI:v6p98/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p98/r8.claim: A report says Adam sneezed, praised God, received God’s blessing, then greeted the assembled angels; God identified this as his greeting and his descendants’ greeting.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r8.anchor: روي : عنه عليه السلام قال : "لما خلق الله تعالى آدم ونفخ فيه الروح عطس فقال : الحمدفقال الله تعالى يرحمك ربك يا آدم

BURSEVI:v6p98/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r9.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p98/r9.claim: A report lists six Muslim duties: greet on meeting, answer an invitation, counsel in absence, bless after a sneeze, visit the sick, and attend the funeral.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r9.anchor: وروي عنه عليه السلام قال : "حق المسلم على المسلم ست يسلم عليه إذا لقيه ويجيبه إذا دعاه وينصح له بالغيب

BURSEVI:v6p98/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p98/r10.claim: In emergencies such as fire, theft, unlawful killing, or an apparent wrong requiring removal, permission and greeting are not required; necessity suspends prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r10.anchor: فحينئذ لا يجب الاستئذان والتسليم فإن كل ذلك مستثنى بالدليل وهو ما قاله الفقهاء من أن مواقع الضرورات مستثناة من قواعد الشرع

BURSEVI:v6p98/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p98/r11.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v6p98/r11.claim: Al-Kashshāf laments that people have abandoned many religious practices as if they were abrogated, including seeking permission.
BURSEVI:v6p98/r11.anchor: قال صاحب "الكشاف" : وكم من باب من أبواب الدين هو عند الناس كالشريعة المنسوخة قد تركوا العمل بها وباب الاستئذان من ذلك

STUDYQURAN:24:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r1.speaker: some commentators (Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r1.claim: Inquiring may mean signaling one's presence by clearing the throat or knocking, so occupants know someone is there before being greeted.
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r1.anchor: Some say inquire and greet the dwellers refers to a signal like clearing one’s throat or knocking at the door

STUDYQURAN:24:27/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r2.claim: The greeting is the formula Peace be upon you.
STUDYQURAN:24:27/r2.anchor: The greeting here is the formula “Peace be upon you”

TAB-FULL:v17p240/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly read “حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا” and called the received wording a scribal error.
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم

TAB-FULL:v17p240/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r2.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash read the phrase as “حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا.”
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r2.anchor: عن الأعمش، أنه " كان يقرؤها: «حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا»

TAB-FULL:v17p240/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains istīʾnās as seeking permission.

TAB-FULL:v17p240/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that Ibn Masʿūd’s codex ordered greeting the household before asking permission.
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، قال: " في مصحف ابن مسعود: «حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا»

TAB-FULL:v17p240/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to read the greeting before the request for permission, treating “تستأنسوا” as a copyist’s error.
TAB-FULL:v17p240/r5.anchor: عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس أنه " كان يقرؤها: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا»

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r1.claim: Mujāhid recounts Ibn ʿUmar greeting a woman and repeatedly asking to enter until she explicitly invited him in.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r1.anchor: قال مغيرة: قال مجاهد: " جاء ابن عمر من حاجة وقد آذاه الرمضاء، فأتى

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r2.claim: The Prophet taught an inept visitor to say, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?” and then admitted him.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأمة له يقال لها روضة " قومي إلى هذا فكلميه، فإنه لا يحسن يستأذن

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says seeking permission was abrogated, with uninhabited houses exempted by 24:29.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس، قوله: {حتى تستأنسوا} [النور: 27] قال: الاستئذان، ثم نسخ , واستثنى:

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm interprets the condition as greeting the household and asking permission.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r4.anchor: عن المغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قوله: {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم} [النور: 27] قال: «حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا»

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses istīʾnās as asking permission and greeting the household.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r5.anchor: أخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة: {حتى تستأنسوا} [النور: 27] قال: «حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا»

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says permission must be sought even when entering one’s mothers’ and sisters’ homes.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r6.anchor: عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود، قال: «عليكم أن تستأذنوا على أمهاتكم وأخواتكم»

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r7.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r7.claim: An Anṣārī woman’s complaint that male relatives entered while she was undressed is given as the occasion for this verse’s revelation.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r7.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت: أن امرأة من الأنصار قالت: " يا رسول الله، إني أكون في منزلي على الحال التي لا أحب أن يراني أحد عليها والد ولا ولد

TAB-FULL:v17p241/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r8.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r8.claim: Another group takes the word to mean alerting household members by clearing the throat, spitting, or similar sounds.
TAB-FULL:v17p241/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: حتى تؤنسوا أهل البيت بالتنحنح والتنخم وما أشبهه، حتى يعلموا أنكم تريدون الدخول عليهم

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains the word as clearing the throat and spitting before entry.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها} [النور: 27] قال: «حتى تتنحنحوا وتتنخموا»

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r2.claim: Mujāhid also glosses the phrase as making a sound and greeting the household.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {حتى تستأنسوا} [النور: 27] قال: «حتى تجرسوا وتسلموا»

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people reject the Qurʾānic rule that the most honored before God are the most pious, not those of highest worldly rank.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " ثلاث آيات قد جحدهن الناس

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās insists that a man ask permission before entering his sisters’ quarters, even in a shared home, to avoid seeing them naked and to obey God.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " ثلاث آيات قد جحدهن الناس

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r5.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r5.claim: Ṭāwūs says he most disliked seeing a close female relative naked and was strict about this rule.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r5.anchor: قال ابن جريج: وأخبرني ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، قال: " ما من امرأة أكره إلي أن أرى كأنه يقول: عريتها أو عريانة من ذات محرم.

TAB-FULL:v17p243/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says everyone who reaches puberty must seek permission, including from one’s mother and female relatives, as 24:59 commands.
TAB-FULL:v17p243/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح: " وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا، فواجب على الناس أجمعين إذا احتلموا أن يستأذنوا

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r1.claim: The Prophet tells a man to ask permission before every entry to his mother’s home because he would not want to see her naked.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار: أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أستأذن على أمي؟ قال: «نعم»

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reiterates that permission must be sought before entering one’s mother’s home.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r2.anchor: أنه سمع ابن مسعود يقول: «عليكم الإذن على أمهاتكم»

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r3.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says a man does not need to ask permission to enter upon his wife.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r3.anchor: قلت لعطاء: " أيستأذن الرجل على امرأته؟ قال: لا "

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r4.speaker: زينب
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r4.claim: Zaynab reports that ʿAbd Allāh would clear his throat and spit at the door to avoid unexpectedly encountering something private.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r4.anchor: عن زينب، قالت: «كان عبد الله إذا جاء من حاجة فانتهى إلى الباب، تنحنح وبزق، كراهة أن يهجم منا على أمر يكرهه»

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd explains istīʾnās as clearing the throat and making a sound so residents know someone has arrived.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قول الله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا} [النور: 27] قال: " الاستئناس: التنحنح والتجرس، حتى يعرفوا أن قد جاءهم أحد.

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers deriving istīʾnās from uns and understands it as requesting entry, announcing oneself, and receiving the household’s assent.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r6.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي أن يقال: إن الاستئناس: الاستفعال من الأنس، وهو أن يستأذن أهل البيت في الدخول عليهم

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites the Arab expression “go and istānis” as meaning to look whether anyone is in the house.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r7.anchor: وقد حكي عن العرب سماعا: اذهب فاستأنس، هل ترى أحدا في الدار؟ بمعنى: انظر هل ترى فيها أحدا؟

TAB-FULL:v17p245/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the wording reverses the intended order: greet the household first, then ask permission.
TAB-FULL:v17p245/r8.anchor: وهو من المقدم الذي معناه التأخير، إنما هو: حتى تسلموا وتستأذنوا، كما ذكرنا من الرواية عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r1.claim: These rulings continue the fitting sequence of legal instructions in the passage.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r1.anchor: بيان أحكام وشرائع متناسبة ومناسبة لما تقدم

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r2.claim: Uns means affinity and a settled heart; istiʾnās is seeking that familiarity by signaling—such as remembering God or clearing one's throat—so a householder knows someone wants to enter.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r2.anchor: الأنس بالشيء وإليه الإلفة وسكون القلب إليه

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r3.claim: The signal lets residents prepare before being seen in a private state; the rule protects their privacy and the dignity of faith.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r3.anchor: فربما كان في حال لا يحب أن يراه عليها أحد أو يطلع عليها مطلع

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r4.claim: Signaling before entry and then greeting the residents helps conceal private matters and reassures them that the visitor poses no threat.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r4.anchor: فأخبر باستيناسه صاحب البيت بدخوله ثم دخل فسلم عليه فقد أعانه على ستر عورته

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r5.claim: Maintaining this practice strengthens brotherhood, affection, and mutual cooperation in showing what is good and covering what is shameful, foundations of social happiness.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r5.anchor: ويؤدي الاستمرار على هذا السيرة الجميلة إلى استحكام الأخوة والإلفة والتعاون العام

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r6.claim: The verse's reminder points to the duties of preserving brotherhood and united hearts through which social well-being is sustained.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r6.anchor: أي لعلكم بالاستمرار على هذه السيرة تتذكرون ما يجب عليكم رعايته وإحياؤه

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r7.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted phrase: the rule was given so people would recall God's admonitions and act accordingly; the author allows this reading.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r7.anchor: وقيل إن قوله { لعلكم تذكرون } تعليل لمحذوف

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r8.claim: A proposed transposition puts greeting before signaling; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r8.anchor: وقيل إن في قوله { حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا } تقديما وتأخيرا

TABATABAI:24:27-29/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r10.claim: The preceding verse covers entry when the person authorized to admit is present and does not refuse; verse 28 covers houses with no such person present.
TABATABAI:24:27-29/r10.anchor: والآية السابقة تبين حكم الدخول وفيه من يملك الإذن ولا يمنع

TABATABAI:24:27-34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r1.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r1.claim: Asked what istiʾnās means, the Prophet says to announce oneself to the household with tasbīḥ, taḥmīd, takbīr, or throat-clearing; al-Durr al-manthūr also transmits this report.
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r1.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال قلنا يا رسول الله ما الاستيناس

TABATABAI:24:27-34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r2.speaker: سهل بن سعد
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r2.claim: When a man peered into one of the Prophet's chambers, the Prophet threatened to pierce his eye with a comb and explained that permission is required to prevent looking; al-Durr al-manthūr also transmits it.
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r2.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال اطلع رجل في حجرة من حجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:24:27-34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r3.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r3.claim: A man asks whether he must seek permission to enter upon his mother each time; the Prophet asks whether he would want to see her naked, and he agrees permission is necessary.
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r3.anchor: قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أستأذن على أمي؟ فقال نعم

TABATABAI:24:27-34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r4.speaker: عمرو بن سعد الثقفي
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r4.claim: After a visitor sought entry by clearing his throat, the Prophet had Rawḍa teach him to say “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”; al-Durr al-manthūr attributes this report to ʿAmr b. Saʿd al-Thaqafī.
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r4.anchor: وروي أن رجلا استأذن على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فتنحنح

TABATABAI:24:27-34/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r5.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r5.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh says that whoever lets his eye enter before asking permission and greeting has disobeyed God and has no permission.
TABATABAI:24:27-34/r5.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سئل عن الاستيذان في البيوت

TABRISI:24:27/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27/r1.claim: Istīnā is seeking familiarity through knowledge or another means; the Arab idiom “go and become familiar” means to find out whether anyone is there.
TABRISI:24:27/r1.anchor: الاستيناس طلب الأنس بالعلم أو غيره تقول العرب اذهب فاستأنس هل ترى أحدا

TABRISI:24:27/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27/r2.claim: The same verb appears in 4:6 with the sense “you know/perceive.”
TABRISI:24:27/r2.anchor: أي علمتم وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال

TABRISI:24:27/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:24:27/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the wording should be “until you seek permission,” rather than “until you seek familiarity.”
TABRISI:24:27/r3.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال إنما هي تستأذنوا

TABRISI:24:27/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TABRISI:24:27/r4.claim: A similar reading with “seek permission” is also transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh.
TABRISI:24:27/r4.anchor: وكذلك يروى عن عبد الله وروي عن أبي

TABRISI:24:27/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r5.speaker: أبي
TABRISI:24:27/r5.claim: A reading transmitted from Ubayy puts greeting before seeking familiarity, and Ibn ʿAbbās is also said to have read it that way.
TABRISI:24:27/r5.anchor: وروي عن أبي حتى تسلموا وتستأنسوا وكذلك قرأ ابن عباس

TABRISI:24:27/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
TABRISI:24:27/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās are reported to say that the written form is a scribal error and that the reading was “until you seek permission.”
TABRISI:24:27/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس قال أخطأ الكاتب فيه وكان يقرأ حتى تستأذنوا

TABRISI:24:27/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r7.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:24:27/r7.claim: Another explanation takes istīnā as throat-clearing and speech that serve the function of asking permission, clarified by the rule for children reaching puberty.
TABRISI:24:27/r7.anchor: تستأنسوا بالتنحنح والكلام الذي يقوم مقام الاستيذان وقد بين الله تعالى ذلك في قوله

TABRISI:24:27/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
TABRISI:24:27/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās explain “seek familiarity” here as seeking permission before entering another person’s house.
TABRISI:24:27/r15.anchor: حتى تستأذنوا عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس

TABRISI:24:27-29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r1.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
TABRISI:24:27-29/r1.claim: Mujāhid and al-Suddī connect the permission sense to the rule that children must ask permission when they reach puberty.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r1.anchor: وإذا بلغ الأطفال منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا [النور: 59] عن مجاهد والسدي

TABRISI:24:27-29/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r2.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
TABRISI:24:27-29/r2.claim: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī reports that the Prophet described announcing oneself with praise, glorification, or throat-clearing.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r2.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال: " قلنا يا رسول الله ما الاستيناس قال:

TABRISI:24:27-29/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r3.speaker: سهل بن سعد
TABRISI:24:27-29/r3.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports that the Prophet warned a man who looked into his room, saying he would have jabbed his scratching tool into the man’s eye; permission exists because of sight.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r3.anchor: وعن سهل بن سعد قال " أطلع رجل في حجرة من حجر رسول الله

TABRISI:24:27-29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27-29/r4.claim: An unnamed man asked whether he must seek permission to enter on his mother; the Prophet said to do so, asking whether he wanted to see her naked.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r4.anchor: وروي أن " رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أستأذن على أمي فقال:

TABRISI:24:27-29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27-29/r5.claim: One parsing puts the actions in a different order: greet the residents, seek familiarity and permission, and enter only if allowed.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r5.anchor: قيل إن فيه تقديما وتأخيرا تقديره حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأنسوا وتستأذنوا فإن أذن لكم فادخلوا

TABRISI:24:27-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27-29/r6.claim: Alternatively, greeting itself creates familiarity; a man once cleared his throat at the Prophet’s door, so the Prophet had Rawḍa teach him to say, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”
TABRISI:24:27-29/r6.anchor: فقد روي أن رجلا استأذن على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتنحنح فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لامرأة يقال لها روضة:

TABRISI:24:27-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27-29/r7.claim: Entering after permission is better for visitors, who should remember God’s teachings, commands, and prohibitions and follow them.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r7.anchor: معناه ذلك الدخول بالاستيذان خير لكم

TABRISI:24:27-29/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:24:27-29/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:24:27-29/r20.claim: The entry rule follows the emphatic condemnation of fornication and slander, keeping people farther from suspicion and closer to innocence from sin.
TABRISI:24:27-29/r20.anchor: وجه اتصال الآية بما قبلها أنه سبحانه لما عظم شأن الزنا والقذف أكد ذلك بالنهي عن دخول بيوت الناس

THALABI:v7p83#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p83#2/r1.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
THALABI:v7p83#2/r1.claim: A woman from the Ansar told the Prophet that her father and other male relatives entered while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the verse was revealed in response.
THALABI:v7p83#2/r1.anchor: حدثنا قيس عن أشعث بن سوار عن عدي بن ثابت

THALABI:v7p83#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p83#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
THALABI:v7p83#2/r2.claim: Some commentators explain tastaʾnisū as asking permission to enter.
THALABI:v7p83#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: حتى تستأنسوا أي تستأذنوا

THALABI:v7p83#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p83#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p83#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the wording should be tastaʾdhinu (ask permission) and that the scribe erred; Ubayy, Ibn Abbas, and al-Aʿmash are also reported to read it that way.
THALABI:v7p83#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إنما هو حتى تستأذنوا ولكن أخطأ الكاتب، وكان أبي بن كعب وابن عباس والأعمش يقرءونها كذلك

THALABI:v7p83#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p83#2/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p83#2/r4.claim: The verse has fronting and delay: its intended order is to greet the household and then ask permission; Ibn Masud's codex has this order.
THALABI:v7p83#2/r4.anchor: وفي الآية تقديم وتأخير تقديرها: حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا، وكذلك هو في مصحف ابن مسعود

THALABI:v7p84/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r1.speaker: عمرو بن سعيد الثقفي
THALABI:v7p84/r1.claim: A man asked the Prophet if he could enter; the Prophet had Rawda teach him to say, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”
THALABI:v7p84/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن سعيد الثقفي أن رجلا استأذن على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أألج

THALABI:v7p84/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r2.speaker: مجاهد، السدي
THALABI:v7p84/r2.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi interpret seeking permission as clearing the throat and spitting to announce one's presence.
THALABI:v7p84/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد والسدي: هو التنحنح والتنخم

THALABI:v7p84/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r3.speaker: زينب
THALABI:v7p84/r3.claim: Zaynab reports that Abd Allah ibn Masud cleared his throat and spat by the door so he would not surprise his family with something unwelcome.
THALABI:v7p84/r3.anchor: عن زينب قالت: كان عبد الله إذا جاء من حاجة فانتهى الى الباب تنحنح وبزق

THALABI:v7p84/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r4.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v7p84/r4.claim: Ikrima says seeking permission can mean saying tasbih, takbir, or the like.
THALABI:v7p84/r4.anchor: عكرمة: هو التسبيح والتكبير ونحو ذلك

THALABI:v7p84/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r5.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
THALABI:v7p84/r5.claim: When asked what istinas means, the Prophet said a person speaks words of remembrance or clears his throat to alert the household.
THALABI:v7p84/r5.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال: قلنا يا رسول الله ما الاستيناس الذي يريد الله سبحانه

THALABI:v7p84/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r6.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v7p84/r6.claim: Al-Khalil glosses istinas as seeking to see or ascertain, connecting it to the phrase “I perceived a fire.”
THALABI:v7p84/r6.anchor: وقال الخليل: الاستيناس: الاستبصار من قوله آنست نارا

THALABI:v7p84/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v7p84/r7.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation explain istinas as seeking familiarity: check whether anyone is home and alert them that you are entering; Arabs say to go and see whether anyone is in the house.
THALABI:v7p84/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: الاستيناس: طلب الأنس وهو أن ينظر هل في البيت أحد يؤذنه أنه داخل عليهم

THALABI:v7p84/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p84/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
THALABI:v7p84/r8.claim: Abu Musa sought entry three times at Umar's home and left; Umar recalled him for evidence, and Abu Musa cited the Prophet's instruction to seek permission three times, then return if not admitted.
THALABI:v7p84/r8.anchor: ويروى أن أبا موسى الأشعري أتى منزل عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنهما فقال: السلام عليكم أأدخل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r1.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r1.claim: A woman from the Anṣār asked the Prophet what to do when male relatives entered while she was in a state in which she did not want to be seen; the verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r1.anchor: روى عدي بن ثابت (¬4) أن امرأة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r2.claim: These are houses that do not belong to you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني بيوتا ليست لكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، مقاتل، قتادة، السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r3.claim: Here tastaʾnisū means ask permission to enter.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r4.claim: Istīdhān is seeking information; istinas means finding out whether residents want the visitor to enter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى {تستأنسوا} في اللغة: تستأذنوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r5.claim: Istīnas is learning who is in the house, as in saying one investigated and found nobody.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: الاستئناس: أن يعلم من في الدار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r6.claim: In Arabic, istīnas can mean looking to see who is in the house.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء: الاستئناس في كلام العرب: النظر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r7.speaker: النابغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r7.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse uses mustaʾnis for a wary creature scanning and turning to check for anything there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r7.anchor: وقول النابغة: بذي الجليل (¬7) على مستأنس وحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the wording should be until you ask permission, and calls tastaʾnisū a copyist's mistake.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r8.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {حتى تستأنسوا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p188#2/r9.claim: They explain istīnas as clearing the throat or sniffling to announce oneself, a kind of seeking information.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r1.claim: They understand the wording by fronting and delaying: greet the residents, then request permission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين. هذا على التقديم والتأخير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r2.claim: The codex of ʿAbd Allāh has the greeting-before-permission order, illustrated by comparable pairs in 3:43 and 64:2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r2.anchor: وكذا هو في مصحف عبد الله مستقيم كقوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r3.claim: Permission is prescribed, entering another's house uninvited is forbidden, and the Sunnah greeting is السلام عليكم أأدخل.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r3.anchor: والسنة فيه أن يقول: السلام عليكم أأدخل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r4.claim: Ask permission three times: the first lets the household hear, the second lets them prepare, and the third lets them admit or refuse; if refused, leave without lingering at their door.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r4.anchor: قال قتادة -في هذه الآية- كان يقال: الاستئذان ثلاث مرات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r5.speaker: أبو موسى عن النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r5.claim: The Prophet says permission is sought three times; if it is not granted, return.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p192/r5.anchor: وقد روى أبو موسى، عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r1.claim: This is purer for you and brings a greater reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أزكى لكم وأعظم لأجوركم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r2.claim: Asking permission is better than entering without it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أفضل لكم من أن تدخلوا بغير إذن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r3.claim: Remember that greeting and asking permission are good and follow them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r3.anchor: أن السلام والاستئذان خير فتأخذون به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r4.claim: It means so that you take admonition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p193/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد كي تتعظوا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r1.claim: Tastaʾnisū means to ask permission before entering.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r1.anchor: حتى تستأنسوا } تستأذنوا { وتسلموا على أهلها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r2.claim: The greeting is to say, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:24:27-30/r2.anchor: تسلموا على أهلها } وهو أن يقول: السلام عليكم، أأدخل؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r6.claim: Qatāda explains istiʾnās here as asking permission to enter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r6.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة قال: وهو الاستئذان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the scribe erred and the phrase should read “until you ask permission and greet the household.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r7.anchor: حدثني أشعث، عن جعفر بن أبي وحشية، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: أخطأ الكاتب، حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا على أهلها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r8.claim: Mujāhid explains the word as clearing one’s throat and spitting to announce one’s presence.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {حتى تستأنسوا} [النور: 27] حتى تنحنحوا وتنخموا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r9.claim: Yaḥyā says the order is advanced and delayed: greet first, then ask permission.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r9.anchor: قال يحيى: وهي مقدمة مؤخرة: حتى تسلموا وتستأذنوا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r10.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r10.claim: A man asks the Prophet whether he may enter; the Prophet has someone teach him proper permission etiquette, and the man then greets and asks permission.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r10.anchor: - الحسن بن دينار، عن محمد بن سيرين أن رجلا استأذن على النبي فقال: أدخل؟ فقال النبي لرجل عنده: قم فعلم هذا كيف يستأذن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r11.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r11.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam recounts Ibn ʿUmar’s instruction: greet, wait for a returned greeting, ask to enter, and enter only after permission.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r11.anchor: - عثمان وإبراهيم بن محمد، عن زيد بن أسلم قال: جئت ابن عمر في بيته فقلت: ألج؟ فأذن لي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r12.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan recounts al-Ashʿarī returning after three unanswered requests; ʿUmar demands proof of the Prophet’s rule and Ṭalḥa witnesses it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r12.anchor: - وحدثني الحسن بن دينار، عن الحسن أن الأشعري استأذن على عمر ثلاثا فلم يؤذن له فرجع،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r13.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r13.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r13.claim: The Prophet’s rule, cited in the report, is that anyone denied entry after asking three times should leave.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p436/r13.anchor: فقال: قال رسول الله: «من استأذن ثلاثا فلم يؤذن له فليرجع» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar used to leave merchants’ homes when they responded to his greeting with “enter in peace.”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r1.anchor: - وحدثني الصلت بن دينار، عن محمد بن سيرين، عن ابن عمر أنه كان إذا جاء إلى بيوت التجار فسلم ليدخل فقيل له: ادخل بسلام، رجع ولم يدخل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p438/r2.claim: The practice is better for you so that you may remember.

ELMALILI:24:27/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r1.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
ELMALILI:24:27/r1.claim: An unnamed woman from the Anṣār complained that a household member sometimes entered while she was in a state in which she did not want to be seen; the verse was revealed in response.

ELMALILI:24:27/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r2.claim: Buyūt includes other people's houses or rooms; one must not enter them before making oneself known and greeting their occupants.
ELMALILI:24:27/r2.anchor: Kendi buyûtunuzun gayrı buyûta evlerinizin gayrı evlere, odalarınızın gayrı odalara

ELMALILI:24:27/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r3.claim: Entering another person's property without permission is a usurpatory transgression, legally and judicially forbidden; even in one's own home, entering another person's room unannounced and without greeting is religiously and ethically prohibited.
ELMALILI:24:27/r3.anchor: âharın milkine izinsiz girmek gasb kabîlinden bir ta‘addî olacağından hukūken ve kazâen haram olduğu gibi kendi milki olan, dinen hakk-ı duhûlü bulunan hane dâhilinde dahi olsa

ELMALILI:24:27/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r4.speaker: istînâsı istîzân diye tefsir edenler
ELMALILI:24:27/r4.claim: Some interpreters understand istīnās to mean seeking permission.
ELMALILI:24:27/r4.anchor: Burada “istînâs”ı istîzân diye tefsir edenler olduğu gibi

ELMALILI:24:27/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r5.speaker: istînâsı istikşâf-ı hâl ile isti‘lâm diye tefsir edenler
ELMALILI:24:27/r5.claim: Others understand istīnās as checking beforehand whether circumstances permit entry or finding out whether anyone is present.
ELMALILI:24:27/r5.anchor: istikşâf-ı hâl ile isti‘lâm, yani istîzândan evvel hâlin girmeye

ELMALILI:24:27/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r6.claim: The apparent meaning is the opposite of startling the occupants: show sociable, humane consideration suited to the circumstances instead of barging in like a wild animal.
ELMALILI:24:27/r6.anchor: “îhâş” mukabili olmasıdır ki baskın eder gibi birdenbire

ELMALILI:24:27/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r7.speaker: Ebû Eyyub
ELMALILI:24:27/r7.claim: When asked what istīnās means, the Prophet reportedly said to notify the household by coughing, saying tasbīḥ, or saying takbīr.
ELMALILI:24:27/r7.anchor: Ebû Eyyub’dan mervîdir ki, “‘yâ Resûlallah! İstînâs nedir?’ dedik, buyurdu ki: ‘Öksürerek, tesbih ve tekbir ile ehl-i beyti haberdar etmektir.’

ELMALILI:24:27/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r8.claim: Taslim means saying al-salāmu ʿalaykum; istīnās is broader than formal permission, encompassing gentle notification and announcement, which explains the verse's wording.
ELMALILI:24:27/r8.anchor: Teslim de “es-selâmü aleyküm” demektir. Şu hâlde “istînâs” sarâhaten istîzân ile mûnisâne ihbar ve ihsastan e‘am olur.

ELMALILI:24:27/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r9.claim: Permission is always required to enter a home where one has no ownership or right of entry; otherwise entry is an assault and the householder may defend himself.
ELMALILI:24:27/r9.anchor: milki olmayan ve hiçbir vechile hakk-ı duhûlü bulunmayan hânelere girmek için her hâlde istîzân şarttır. Yoksa bir taarruz ve tecavüz olur.

ELMALILI:24:27/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r10.claim: Where one has a right to enter but another person occupies the room, making oneself known is required; asking permission specifically is sunnah or etiquette rather than obligatory.
ELMALILI:24:27/r10.anchor: başkasının sâkin bulunduğu odaya girmekte ise mutlak istînâs şart ve fakat bu istînâsın istîzân suretinde olması sünnet veya edeb olmakla beraber farz denilemez.

ELMALILI:24:27/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r11.claim: A judge who must enter a criminal's or suspect's home need not seek permission, but should still announce himself to avoid violating the occupant's honor.
ELMALILI:24:27/r11.anchor: bir hâkim tarafından bir mücrim veya müttehemin meskenine girmek iktizâ ettiği zaman da “istîzân” denilemezse de ırza bir tecavüz vaziyetine düşülmemek için istînâs edilmelidir.

ELMALILI:24:27/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r12.claim: Homes must be protected from intrusion and indecency, and their residents' security and peace respected by entering with proper etiquette through announcement and greeting.
ELMALILI:24:27/r12.anchor: Hâsılı meskenler taarruzdan ve edebsizlikten masûn tutulmalıdır. Hiç kimsenin meskeninde emniyet ve huzûru ihlâl edilmemeli

ELMALILI:24:27/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r13.speaker: رسول الله
ELMALILI:24:27/r13.claim: A visitor who asked to enter using the blunt phrase “shall I penetrate?” was taught to say “peace be upon you; may I enter?”; only after repeating the proper formula was he admitted.
ELMALILI:24:27/r13.anchor: Aleyhisselâtü vesselâm da Ravza namında bir kadına “kalk şuna öğret, istîzânı güzel yapmıyor

ELMALILI:24:27/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r14.speaker: رسول الله
ELMALILI:24:27/r14.claim: In the same report, the Prophet says that although God granted him much good, some knowledge is known only to God, and recites Luqmān 31:34.
ELMALILI:24:27/r14.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm da “Allah teâlâ bana bir hayr-ı kesîr ihsan etti, ma‘amâfîh hiç şüphe yok ilimden[^8] öylesi vardır ki onu Allah’tan başkası bilmez” buyurmuş ve إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلْمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ [Lokman 31/34]

ELMALILI:24:27/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r15.claim: Pre-Islamic visitors disregarded the sanctity of the home and used greetings limited to morning or evening well-wishing; such greetings are not inherently bad, but reflect a horizon confined to worldly social wishes.
ELMALILI:24:27/r15.anchor: Câhiliye ahâlisi birinin evine vardıklarında harem saygısı gözetmedikleri gibi dünya ve âhiret selâmetine şâmil olan selâm duasını bilmezler de

ELMALILI:24:27/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r16.claim: God teaches salām as a concise greeting promising unlimited well-being, broad enough to be the highest shared social ideal; relying only on other greetings instead is disliked as a remnant of jāhiliyya.
ELMALILI:24:27/r16.anchor: Allah teâlâ, istînâsı şart kıldığı gibi mü’minlere nâmahdud bir selâmet hissi va‘d ü telkin eden selâmı tâlim ile lafzı veciz, mânası vâsi‘ve herkes için gāye-i matlab olacak en güzel bir şi‘âr-ı ictimâ‘î teşrî‘buyurmuştur.

ELMALILI:24:27/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r17.claim: Because salām is taught as the prescribed greeting, withholding it and relying on other greetings alone is makrūh.
ELMALILI:24:27/r17.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bunu dirîğ ederek diğer tahiyyelerle iktifâ etmek bir câhiliyet eseri olacağı cihetle mekruhtur.

ELMALILI:24:27/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r18.speaker: رسول الله
ELMALILI:24:27/r18.claim: Permission is sought three times: the first gives the household notice, the second allows them to prepare, and the third brings permission or refusal; after no answer at the third request, the visitor should leave.
ELMALILI:24:27/r18.anchor: Resûlullah’tan rivayet olunduğuna göre istîzân üçtür. Birincisinde kulak verirler, ikincisinde hazırlanırlar. Üçüncüsünde izin verirler veya reddederler.

ELMALILI:24:27/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r19.claim: The three requests should be spaced rather than made one after another, and the visitor should leave if no answer comes to the third.
ELMALILI:24:27/r19.anchor: Bu üç istîzân birbiri ardı sıra vely ettirilmeyip aralarında biraz fâsıla ile yapılmalı ve üçüncüsünde cevap verilmezse dönmelidir.

ELMALILI:24:27/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r20.claim: Loudly pounding on the door or shouting at the residents is forbidden because it disturbs and frightens them; al-Ḥujurāt 49:4 is sufficient prohibition in this matter.
ELMALILI:24:27/r20.anchor: Şiddetle kapı çalmak, hâne sâhibine bağırmak ise haramdır. Zira îzâ ve îhâşı tazammun eder, yürek oynatır. Bu babda nâzil olan إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَٰتِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ [el-Hucurât 49/4]

ELMALILI:24:27/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r21.claim: The Prophet used to stand to the right or left of the door rather than directly facing it while seeking permission.
ELMALILI:24:27/r21.anchor: Hem de istîzân ederken yüzünü kapıya karşı tutup durmamalı, sağa veya[^15] sola teveccüh etmelidir.

ELMALILI:24:27/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r22.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd Hudrî
ELMALILI:24:27/r22.claim: When Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī sought permission while facing the door, the Prophet told him not to do so.
ELMALILI:24:27/r22.anchor: Ebû Sa‘îd Hudrî radıyallahu anh kapıya müteveccihen istîzân etmişti, Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm لا تستأذن وأنت مستقبل الباب “kapıyı istikbal ederek istîzân etme” buyurdu.

ELMALILI:24:27/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r23.claim: The practice protects visitors from suspicion, strengthens public security and order, and increases chastity and purity.
ELMALILI:24:27/r23.anchor: Bir töhmete düşmekten sâlim kılar; emniyet ve âsâyişi takviye, iffet ü nezâheti tezyid eder.

ELMALILI:24:27/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:24:27/r24.claim: Tadhakkur means to remember, understand, and not forget.
ELMALILI:24:27/r24.anchor: Gerektir ki tezekkür edersiniz düşünür, anlar, unutmazsınız.

ELMALILI:24:27/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:24:27/r25.speaker: رسول الله
ELMALILI:24:27/r25.claim: When a man asked whether he must seek permission before entering his mother's room, the Prophet said yes; when he protested that he alone served her, the Prophet asked whether he wished to see her naked, and told him to ask permission.
ELMALILI:24:27/r25.anchor: bir adam “anama da istîzân edecek miyim?” dedi, “evet” buyurdu. “Onun benden başka hizmet edeni yok, her girişimde istîzân mı edeyim?” dedi, Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm “ananı üryan görmek arzu eder misin?” buyurdu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r1.claim: Rules for entering others' homes are placed after the ban on slander about chastity and before protective measures because they connect by cause and effect to both topics.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r1.anchor: İffet ve namusla ilgili iftirayı yasaklayan, bu davranışın ne kadar büyük bir günah ve ağır bir suç teşkil ettiğini açıklayan âyetlerden sonra

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r2.claim: Ignoring entry etiquette can provoke suspicion and spying, expose family secrets, and create forbidden feelings or intentions immediately or later.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r2.anchor: suizanna kapılmaları ve tecessüs duygularının tahrik edilmesi hem de girip çıkanların bazı aile sırlarına vâkıf olmaları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r3.claim: Modern buildings often let residents speak with visitors, ask who they are, and see them before deciding whether to open the door.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r3.anchor: elektriğin ve elektronik araçların bulunduğu binalarda oturanlar, gelenlerle konuşmak, kimliklerini sormak, hatta onları görmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r4.claim: Where such means are unavailable, visitors must follow the proper etiquette themselves and avoid discourteous ways of entering.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r4.anchor: Böyle imkânların bulunmaması halinde kapıya gelenin bazı kurallara kendiliğinden riayet etmesi ve edebe aykırı yollara tevessül etmemesi gerekir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r5.claim: No separate permission is needed for unoccupied or public places open to everyone, such as inns, hotels, public washrooms, and shops.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r5.anchor: hanlar, kervansaraylar, oteller, abdesthaneler, dükkânlar gibi her isteyenin girip çıkmasına, oturup kalkmasına, alışveriş yapmasına açık bulunan yerlere girmek için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r6.claim: The phrase translated as containing one's own belongings can also mean places made available for one's use; the listed public places fit this sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r6.anchor: “İçinde kendinize ait eşya bulunan” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz ifadeyi, “faydalanmanıza açık bulunan” şeklinde de anlamak mümkündür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r7.claim: Under the belongings translation, the phrase can describe buildings abandoned by their owners where others have placed items such as fuel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r7.anchor: sahipleri tarafından terkedilmiş ve içine başkaları tarafından yakacak vb. eşya konmuş binalar ve yerlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r8.claim: In the pre-Islamic period and early Islam, people exchanged greetings but often ignored etiquette, barged into homes, and caused frequent discomfort.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r8.anchor: Câhiliye dönemiyle İslâm’ın ilk yıllarında insanlar birbirlerinin evine girerken “iyi sabahlar, iyi akşamlar” gibi iltifat ifadeleri kullanmakla birlikte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r9.claim: Qur'anic verses and hadith later set specific rules for seeking and granting permission to protect homes' privacy and the dignity of individuals and families.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r9.anchor: konumuz olan âyetler ile diğer âyet ve hadislerde evlere girerken izin isteme ve izin verme konularında özel hükümler getirilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r10.claim: Except for public exceptions or places explicitly opened by their owner or an authorized person, one may not enter private spaces without permission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r10.anchor: özel ve mahrem mekanlara izin almadan girilemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r11.speaker: hadis
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r11.claim: A hadith exempts someone invited to arrive at a specified place and time from seeking permission again when entering then.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r11.anchor: belli bir zamanda bir yere gelmesi için davet edilen kişinin belirtilen zamanda o yere girmesi için izin alması gerekmediği ifade edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r12.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r12.claim: The Prophet's rule is to request entry no more than three times and leave if no permission is given.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r12.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in belirlediği bir kurala göre bir yere girmek için izin isteyen kişi, bu isteğini en çok üç defa tekrar etmeli

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r13.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r13.claim: Kurtubi allows asking more than three times when the visitor thinks the people inside did not hear.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r13.anchor: sesinin duyulmadığını düşünen kimsenin izin talebini üçten fazla tekrar edebileceği belirtilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
