KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r14.claim: The verse also requires greeting the household when asking permission; the Prophet usually greeted and identified himself as he asked.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r14.anchor: 27. âyette izin isterken ev halkına ayrıca selâm verilmesi de istenmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r15.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r15.claim: The Prophet is reported to have usually greeted the household and identified himself while requesting permission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r15.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in böyle durumlarda genellikle selâm verip kendisini tanıtarak izin istediği bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r16.speaker: Nevevî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r16.claim: Although the verse places greeting after the permission request, Nawawi reports that this order is not binding and one may greet and identify oneself first.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r16.anchor: âyetteki sıranın bağlayıcı olmadığı, duruma göre önce selâm verip kendini tanıttıktan sonra izin istemenin mümkün olduğu görüşü de vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r17.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r17.claim: The Prophet told someone who entered without permission to go out and say, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r17.anchor: “Dışarı çık, ‘Selâmün aleyküm, girebilir miyim?’ de” şeklinde uyarırken önce selâmı zikrettiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r18.claim: A visitor requesting entry should identify themselves clearly; the rule also applies when using a knocker, bell, or intercom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r18.anchor: İzin isteyen kişi içeridekilere kendisini açıkça tanıtmalıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r19.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r19.claim: When a visitor answered “It's me” after being asked who he was, the Prophet objected and stressed that the visitor must identify himself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r19.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem, içeri girmek isteyen birine kim olduğunu sorunca bu kişinin “benim” demesine canı sıkılmış, “Sen de kimsin!” diyerek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r20.claim: Even with good intentions, it is forbidden to peer through a door or window into a place one may not enter without permission; the rule protects family privacy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r20.anchor: Bir kimsenin izinsiz girmesi câiz olmayan yeri iyi niyetle de olsa kapı aralığından veya pencereden gözetlemesi de câiz değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r21.claim: The ban on believers spying on one another's private affairs in 49:12 is also relevant to the prohibition on peeping into homes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r21.anchor: Müminlerin casusluk yapar gibi birbirlerinin mahrem durumlarını araştırmalarını yasaklayan âyetin (Hucurât 49/12) bu konuyla da ilgili olduğu kabul edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r22.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r22.claim: The Prophet sharply admonished someone he saw peering into a home.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:24:27/r22.anchor: Hz. Peygamber, birinin bu şekilde evini gözetlediğini görünce onu sert bir dille uyarmıştır

QUSHAYRI:v2p363/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p363/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p363/r8.claim: Do not enter an unoccupied home without permission: this preserves God's command and the owner's privacy, since someone may be exposed or guarding a private matter.
QUSHAYRI:v2p363/r8.anchor: في هذا حفظ أمر الله وحفظ حرمة صاحب الدار ؛ لأن من دخلها بغير إذن صاحبها ربما تكون فيها عورة

BURHAN:v3p279/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r12.claim: The verse is included among the section's examples of unusual word order; this excerpt gives no separate gloss.

ITQAN:v2p540/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p540/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p540/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the written تستأنسوا is a scribal error for تستأذنوا, meaning ask permission before entering.
ITQAN:v2p540/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا ﴾ قال إنما هي خطأ من الكاتب

ITQAN:v2p542/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p542/r7.speaker: ابن أشته
ITQAN:v2p542/r7.claim: Ibn Ashte reconciles these reports by saying scribes selected a less preferred form among the seven ahruf, not text outside the Quran; claims of a scribal mistake describe a failure to choose or consider the best option.
ITQAN:v2p542/r7.anchor: وقد أجاب ابن أشته عن هذه الآثار كلها بأن المراد أخطئوا في الاختيار وما هو الأولى لجمع الناس عليه من الأحرف السبعة

ITQAN:v2p542/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p542/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ITQAN:v2p542/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari leans toward weakening the reports because other reports affirm these readings; the author judges Ibn Ashte’s harmonization more apt and better grounded.
ITQAN:v2p542/r8.anchor: وأما ابن الأنباري فإنه جنح إلى تضعيف الروايات ومعارضتها بروايات أخر

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r4.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r4.claim: The entry rule is called ambiguous because it addresses believers and forbids a sin without stating the threat that appears in another ruling about wrongful acts.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r4.anchor: والمتشابه مثل ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا ﴾ الآية ولم يقل ﴿ ومن يفعل ذلك عدوانا وظلما فسوف نصليه نارا ﴾

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r1.claim: A person who denies needing detailed knowledge of Arabic for the Qurʾān, the Prophet’s reports, and language must embrace an unreasonable claim; basic grammar alone does not suffice.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r1.anchor: حاجة في كتاب الله تعالى ، وفي خبر رسول الله ، وفي معرفة الكلام جملة إلى شيء من ذلك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r2.claim: Explaining the nominative in the phrase al-ṣābiʾūn in 5:69 requires the scholars’ analysis and their poetic evidence, including the line beginning وإلا فاعلموا.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r2.anchor: وإلى استشهادهم بقول الشاعر ، + الوافر + : ( وإلا فاعلموا أنا وأنتم بغاة ما بقينا في شقاق )

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r3.claim: The greater harm comes when people who neglect linguistic learning still attempt tafsīr and taʾwīl, producing confused interpretation and building arguments without knowledge.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p44/r3.anchor: جلبوا من الداء ما أعيى الطبيب ، وحير اللبيب ، وانتهى التخليط بما أتوه فيه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p158/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p158/r1.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p158/r1.claim: A woman of the Ansar asked how to protect her privacy when relatives entered her home while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the permission verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p158/r1.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت جاءت إمرأة من الأنصار فقالت يا رسول الله إني أكون في بيتي على حال

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p324/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p324/r1.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p324/r1.claim: An Ansari woman asked how to manage when her father and other relatives entered her home while she was in a state she did not wish them to see; the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p324/r1.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت قال: جاءت امرأة من الأنصار فقالت:

DAMGHANI:v1p80/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p80/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p80/r5.claim: بيوت means homes or residences in the command not to enter another's home without permission.
DAMGHANI:v1p80/r5.anchor: فوجه منها : البيوت بمعنى المنازل . قوله تعالى في سورة النور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r2.claim: A man’s ahl are his household; manzil āhil describes a home with its people, and the verb can mean to marry.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r2.anchor: ويقال : منزل آهل إذا كان به أهله . وأهل فلان ، يأهل ويأهل أهولا : إذا تزوج

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r1.claim: A bayt is a shelter from heat and cold; in settled construction it is a walled plot with a roof, while nomads use a circular wool structure with a matching roof.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r1.anchor: البيت : ما يأوي إليه الإنسان ليقيه الحر والبرد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r2.claim: Some say bayt is named for being suitable for spending the night; bayāt and tabyīt refer to a night attack, and bāta means doing something at night.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r2.anchor: وقيل : سمي بيتا لأنه يصلح للبيتوتة فيه . والبيات والتبييت أن يأتي العدو ليلا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r3.claim: Bayyata al-amr means planning a matter at night; buyūt can mean a troubling concern occupying its owner.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r3.anchor: والبيوت : الأمر يبيت عليه صاحبه ، مهتما به

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r4.speaker: الشاعر
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r4.claim: The unnamed poet’s line uses bayyatū for a plan made at night.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r4.anchor: أتوني فلم أرض ما بيتوا … وكانوا أتوني بشيء نكر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r5.speaker: الهذلي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r5.claim: The Hudhalī poet uses buyūt for a distressing matter one fears.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r6.claim: Bayt can mean an ordinary built house or dwelling.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p205/r6.anchor: منه قوله تعالى في النور : ﴿ لا تدخلوا بيوتا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r1.claim: Tastanisū means seek permission; istiʾnās is finding out whether anyone is in the house.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r1.anchor: {حتى تستأنسوا} أي حتى تستأذنوا {وتسلموا} والاستئناس: أن يعلم من في الدار.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r2.claim: The verb can mean to inquire and ascertain, as in 4:6, where knowing maturity is required.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r2.anchor: ومنه: {فإن آنستم منهم رشدا} (1) أي علمتم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r3.speaker: النابغة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha uses mustaʾnis for a bull that noticed something and became frightened.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p303/r3.anchor:
قال النابغة:
كأن رحلي وقد زال النهار بنا ... بذي الجليل على مستأنس وحد (2) يعني ثورا أبصر شيئا فهو فزع.

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r1.claim: Istīʾnās can mean relieving the visitor’s unease about whether permission will be granted, and thus serves as a synonym for seeking permission.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r1.anchor: لأن الطارق يستوحش من أنه: هل يؤذن له أو لا؟ فيزال استيحاشه

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r2.claim: An alternative derives the word from seeing or perceiving, meaning to ascertain the situation before entering.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r2.anchor: وقيل: من الإيناس وهو الإبصار أي: حتى تستكشفوا الحال

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glossed the expression as “until you seek permission”; this is an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r3.anchor: وفسره ابن عباس " حتى تستأذنوا " وليست قراءة

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r4.claim: The claim attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās that the written form was a scribal mistake for tastaʾdhinū is fabricated against him.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r4.anchor: وما ينقل عنه أنه قال: " تستأنسوا خطأ من الكاتب

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r5.claim: The question resembles the earlier discussion of yaʾs in “Have the believers not despaired?”
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r5.anchor: وهو نظير ما تقدم في الرعد أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r6.claim: Istīʾnās can mean seeking information; the cited verse of poetry uses mustaʾnis for an observer keeping watch.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r6.anchor: 3440 كأن رحلي وقد زال النهار بنا

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r7.claim: A further derivation connects the word to al-uns: ascertain whether anyone is inside.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو من الإنس بكسر الهمزة أي: يتعرف

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r8.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī relates the explanation “make yourselves feel at ease.”
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r8.anchor: وحكى الطبري أنه بمعنى: وتؤنسوا أنفسكم

SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verb’s morphology rules out deriving it from ānasa.
SAMIN-DURR:24:27/r9.anchor: تصريف الفعل يأبى أن يكون من آنس

ZAJJAJ:v4p38/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p38/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p38/r6.claim: Buyutan is read with ḍamma or kasra on the initial consonant; ḍamma is more common and follows the regular plural pattern, while Basrans judge the kasra very poor because fuʿul does not occur with initial kasra in Arabic.
ZAJJAJ:v4p38/r6.anchor: يقرأ بالضم والكسر، ولكن الضم أكثر، فمن ضم فعلى أصل الجمع

ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r1.claim: Tastaʾnisu means seek permission, as in tafsir; istiʾdhan is seeking information or assurance.
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r1.anchor: معنى تستأنسوا في اللغة تستأذنوا، وكذلك هو في التفسير، والاستئذان الاستعلام

ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r2.claim: The related verbs آذن and آنس can mean inform and know, as in فإن آنستم منهم رشدا; therefore the phrase asks whether residents want the visitor to enter.

ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p38#2/r3.claim: The next verse confirms that entry requires permission when nobody is found inside.

ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r1.claim: The categorical ban connects with the preceding passages by adding protection against possible slander.
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r1.anchor: This categorical prohibition connects with the preceding passages inasmuch as it serves as an additional protection of individuals against possible slander.

ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r2.claim: The rule establishes each person's home and private life as inviolable, with wider socio-political implications.
ASAD-NOTES:24:27#n33/r2.anchor: In its wider purport, it postulates the inviolability of each person's home and private life.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r2.claim: In the house-entry verse, isti'nās is not merely asking permission, as some exegetes thought; it means sensing the household's presence and becoming familiar with its people before entering.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r2.anchor: الاستئناس فيها ليس مجرد استئذان كما وهم الذين فسروه بذلك، وإنما هو حس الإيناس لأهل البيت قبل دخوله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.claim: The Arabic sense of īnās is not a bare formal permission, and ānasa is unsuitable for seeing an enemy or fire or hearing thunder or a beast's roar.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p218/r3.anchor: ولا يسوغ في ذوق العربية أن يقال مثلاً: استأنس الرشطي، أو جابى الضرائب، أو الجائن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p317/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p317/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p317/r1.claim: Islahi introduces the instructions in 24:27–34 as something to read against the preceding background of practices that produce social unity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p317/r1.anchor: unity are produced in the society.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r1.claim: Islahi takes istiʾnās here to mean introducing oneself before entering another person’s home.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r2.claim: Buyūt means residential houses where a person’s family lives, as clarified by the following verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r2.anchor: residential houses – as explained in the next verse – where a person’s family lives.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r3.claim: Visitors must not barge into others’ homes: they should introduce themselves with salām at the door, enter only after a response and permission, and otherwise return.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r3.anchor: If they receive a response and are granted permission, only then they should enter the house, otherwise they should return.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r4.claim: Salām is a gracious way both to introduce oneself and to seek permission to enter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p318/r4.anchor: Saying salām is a very gracious way to introduce one’s self and to seek permission

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r1.claim: The greeting lets residents know who is visiting and why, so they can judge whether entry is suitable and whether the timing is appropriate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r1.anchor: through this greeting the residents will come to know of the identity of the person and his purpose of coming

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r2.claim: Seeking leave before entering was customary among civilized peoples and pre-Islamic Arab nobility; Islahi says Islam directed people to use salām for this purpose instead of adopting their wording.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r2.anchor: Amongst the nobility of the Arab jāhiliyyah this tradition also existed; in fact, the words that were used for this had almost the same meaning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r3.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r3.claim: The Prophet taught visitors to say salām at the front door, repeat it three times if there is no answer, and then leave.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r3.anchor: The way taught by the Prophet (sws) to do this was that a person should say this word at the front door

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r4.claim: The restriction prevents an unsuitable visitor from reaching the part of the home where women reside at an inappropriate time; only relatives of the household head or people he fully trusts may enter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r4.anchor: only those people could enter the house who were either related to the head of the family or were fully trusted by him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r5.claim: The reminder explains why the restriction is beneficial rather than burdensome: visitors are entering someone’s privacy and must observe decorum, while residents also benefit by observing the visit’s limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p319/r5.anchor: this word is like a blessed reminder to the person who is visiting that he is intruding into the privacy of someone where he must follow certain decorum.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p320/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p320/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p320/r6.claim: Permission to enter a home where women are present is a relief for relatives and people trusted by the household head, especially since homes then and now may lack a separate men’s reception area.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p320/r6.anchor: only to provide relief regarding the relatives and people of trust of the head of the house.

QIRAAT-ER:24:27:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:7#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:7#1/r1.claim: Kasra rather than ḍamma on bāʾ is an attested dialectal pronunciation of the broken plural without semantic effect.
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:7#1/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on bāʾ instead of ḍamma — dialectal pronunciation of the broken plural, no semantic impact

QIRAAT-ER:24:27:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:9#1/r1.claim: A kasra on bāʾ yields biyūt beside buyūt as a dialectal broken-plural pattern, with no change in meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:9#1/r1.anchor: ḍamma to kasra on bāʾ; dialectal variation in broken plural pattern

QIRAAT-ER:24:27:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:20#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:20#1/r1.claim: Assimilation merges the two tāʾs into a doubled dhāl; the heavier sound emphasizes remembrance without changing the meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:24:27:20#1/r1.anchor: Full assimilation variant: both tāʾs merge into dhāl with shaddah

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p55#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p55#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p55#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses seeking familiarity as asking permission and greeting the household.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p55#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ حتى تستأنسوا ﴾ قال تستأذنوا وتسلموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r1.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r1.claim: A woman from the Anṣār complained that male relatives kept entering her home while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r1.anchor: جاءت امرأة من الأنصار إلى رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r3.claim: The rule follows the slander episode: seclusion gave slanderers an opening, so entering another person’s house requires permission and greeting to prevent suspicion and harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r3.anchor: هو أن أهل الإفك إنما وجدوا السبيل إلى بهتانهم من حيث اتفقت الخلوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān takes the wording to imply that a person may enter their own home without asking permission or greeting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r4.anchor: والظاهر أنه يجوز للإنسان أن يدخل بيت نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r5.speaker: رجل غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r5.claim: A man asked whether he must seek permission before entering on his mother, though he was her only attendant; the Prophet asked whether he wanted to see her naked, and he said no.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p29/r5.anchor: ويروى أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r1.claim: The apparent sense of istīʾnās is relief from unease: a person knocking does not know whether entry will be permitted and becomes at ease after permission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن الاستئناس هو خلاف الاستيحاش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r2.claim: The wording parallels the rule that one must not enter the Prophet’s houses except with permission; istīʾnās is a metonym and follow-on expression for permission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r2.anchor: كقوله: لا تدخلوا بيوت النبي إلا أن يؤذن لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to gloss تستأنسوا as “seek permission.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r3.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال تستأنسوا معناه تستأذنوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān condemns as heretical the claim that Ibn ʿAbbās called تستأنسوا a copyist’s error and read تستأذنوا; he declares Ibn ʿAbbās innocent of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r4.anchor: ومن روي عن ابن عباس أن قوله تستأنسوا خطأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r5.claim: The word تستأنسوا is sound and meaningful in Arabic according to its intended usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r5.anchor: وتستأنسوا متمكنة في المعنى بنية الوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r6.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r6.claim: The report that ʿUmar asked “May I seek comfort, Messenger of God?” at the room’s door shows the word can mean seeking familiarity with him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r6.anchor: وقد قال عمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أستأنس يا رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r7.claim: Another explanation derives the word from inquiry: ascertain whether entry is wanted, as in asking whether anyone is visible or saying one looked and saw nobody.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو من الاستئناس الذي هو الاستعلام والاستكشاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r8.speaker: النابغة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r8.claim: Al-Nābigha’s phrase “على مستأنس وحد” is cited for the sense of someone who can be seen or found alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r8.anchor: ومنه بيت النابعة: كأن رحلي وقد زال النهار بنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r9.claim: A further possibility derives the word from uns: check whether a human being is present.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الأنس وهو أن يتعرف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r10.speaker: أبو أيوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r10.claim: Abū Ayyūb reports that the Prophet said istīʾnās is alerting a household by saying tasbīḥ or takbīr or clearing one’s throat; greeting means saying “peace be upon you.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r10.anchor: وعن أبي أيوب قال: قلنا: يا رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r11.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, a visitor might call out a morning or evening greeting and enter, potentially finding a man with his wife under one blanket; God prevented this and taught better etiquette.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r11.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يقول الرجل منهم إذا دخل بيتا غير بيته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r12.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says visitors should alert the household by clearing the throat, asking permission, or similar means, and ensure the household noticed them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r12.anchor: وذهب الطبري في تستأنسوا إلى أنه بمعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues that the verb’s morphology prevents deriving it from آنس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r13.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وتصريف الفعل يأبى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r14.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r14.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says permission is obligatory for every adult; Abū Ḥayyān’s apparent ruling requires permission generally and considers one request sufficient.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p30/r14.anchor: وقال عطاء: الاستئذان واجب على كل محتلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r1.claim: After prohibitions against zina and accusing chaste women, the passage addresses conduct that could lead to either and teaches manners conducive to happiness.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r1.anchor: إثر ما فصل الزواجر عن الزنا وعن رمي العفائف عنه شرع في تفصيل الزواجر عما عسى يؤدي إلى أحدهما

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r2.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r2.claim: An unnamed Ansari woman asked what to do when visitors entered during a private state that even children or parents should not see; the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r2.anchor: عن رجل من الأنصار أن امرأة قالت : يا رسول الله إني أكون في بيتي على الحالة التي لا أحب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r3.claim: The possessive connection to your homes may express ownership; describing other homes reflects customary residence, though tenants and borrowers also need permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133/r3.anchor: وإضافة البيوت إلى ضمير المخاطبين لامية اختصاصية والمراد عند بعض الاختصاص الملكي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r1.claim: Some understand your homes as homes where you reside, not homes you own; tenants and borrowers also need permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد : اختصاص السكنى أي غير بيوتكم التي تسكنونها لأن الآجر والمعير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r2.claim: A reading pronounces buyutan with kasra on the first letter because of the following ya.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r2.anchor: وقريء ( بيوتا غير بيوتكم ) بكسر الباء لأجل الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to explain seeking familiarity as seeking permission from those authorized to grant it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r3.anchor: وتفسيره بذلك أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم وابن الأنباري في المصاحف وابن جرير وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r4.claim: A report with numerous routes says Ibn Abbas called the written wording a scribal error and said it should read until you ask permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r4.anchor: قال في ( حتى تستأنسوا ) أخطأ الكتاب وإنما هي ( حتى تستأذنوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan condemns anyone who transmits the alleged statement as an enemy of Islam and says Ibn Abbas is innocent of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو حيان : من روي عن ابن عباس إنه قال ذلك فهو طاعن في الإسلام ملحد في الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r6.speaker: الضياء والسخاوي والسيوطي وابن رجب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi counters that the report has many routes and appears in al-Diya's respected Mukhtara, praised as proofworthy or sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r6.anchor: لكن للخبر المذكور طرق كثيرة وكتاب الأحاديث المختارة للضياء كتاب معتبر

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari answers reports that appear to challenge the Qur'an's mass-transmitted text by calling them weak and contradicted by other reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r7.anchor: وابن الأنباري أجاب عن هذا الخبر ونحوه من الأخبار الطاعنة بحسب الظاهر في تواتر القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r8.speaker: ابن أشتة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ashtah explains the reported error as a mistaken choice among the seven modes, with the incorrectly written form outside the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r8.anchor: وأجاب ابن أشتة عن جميع ذلك بأن المراد الخطأ في الاختيار وترك ما هو الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r9.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r9.claim: Al-Suyuti prefers Ibn Ashtah's explanation as more apt; al-Alusi says it strains Ibn Abbas's apparent words and conflicts with the Companions' agreement after the final review.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r9.anchor: واختار الجلال السيوطي هذا الجواب وقال : هو أولى وأقعد من جواب ابن الأنباري

ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r10.claim: Istinas can derive from perceiving or knowing; seeking familiarity means seeking information about whether entry is wanted.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p133#2/r10.anchor: واستعمال الإستثناء بمعنى الإستئذان بناء على أنه استفعال من آنس الشيء بالمد علمه أو أبصره

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r1.claim: Another interpretation derives istinas from intimacy, the opposite of alienation: it means permission, figuratively describing relief when uncertainty is resolved.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r1.anchor: وقيل الإستئناس خلاف الإستيحاش فهو من الإنس بالضم خلاف الوحشة والمراد به المأذونية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r2.claim: Some derive the term from al-ins, people, meaning to find out who is home; the author objects that knowing the occupants does not authorize entry.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r2.anchor: وقيل : الإسنئناس من الإنس بالكسر بمعنى الناس أي تطلبوا معرفة في البيوت من الإنس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r3.claim: Supporters link the people-in-the-house reading to the next verse's case of finding no one there, but the author says this does not overcome the objections.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من رجحه بمناسبته لقوله تعالى ( فإن لم تجدوا فيها أحدا )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r4.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says visitors should make the household aware of them and learn that they have been noticed; the author finds this flawed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r4.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن المعنى حتى تؤنسوا أهل البيت من أنفسكم بالإستئذان ونحوه وتؤنسوا أنفسكم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r5.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r5.claim: Abu Ayyub reports the Prophet defining istinas as a visitor's tasbih, takbir, tahmid, or throat-clearing to notify occupants.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r5.anchor: عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري أنه قال : يا رسول الله ما الإستئناس فقال : يتكلم الرجل بالتسبيحة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the term as clearing one's throat or spitting to notify the household.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r6.anchor: وما أخرجه ابن المنذر وجماعة عن مجاهد أنه قال تستأنسوا تنحنحوا وتنخموا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r7.claim: A further explanation is that visitors notify the household through tasbih or a similar signal; the reports do not rule out earlier interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد حتى تؤنسوا أهل البيت بإعلامهم بالتسبيح أو نحوه والخبران المذكوران لا يأبيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r8.claim: The people addressed by the greeting are the residents of the homes.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r8.anchor: أي الساكنين فيها وظاهر الآية أم الإستئذان قيل التسليم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r9.claim: The apparent order of the verse, as some read it, places asking permission before greeting.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r9.anchor: وظاهر الآية أم الإستئذان قيل التسليم وبه قال بعضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r10.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r10.claim: Al-Nawawi prefers greeting before asking permission, citing reports that greetings precede speech and an un-greeted visitor is not admitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r10.anchor: وقال النووي : الصحيح المختار تقديم التسليم على الإستئذان

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r11.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying that greeting comes before speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r11.anchor: أخرج الترمذي عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله تعالى عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم السلام قبل الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra says someone asking permission before greeting should not be admitted until he greets.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r12.anchor: وابن أبي شيبة والبخاري في الأدب المفرد عن أبي هريرة فيمن يستأذن قبل أن يسلم قال : لا يؤذن له حتى يسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r13.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r13.claim: Zayd b. Aslam recounts Ibn Umar teaching his father to greet first and then ask to enter.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p134/r13.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال : أرسلني أبي إلى ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما فجئته

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Umar sought entry to the Prophet's home by greeting and then asking whether he could enter.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : استأذن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه : على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r2.speaker: الماوردي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r2.claim: Al-Mawardi says greet first if the visitor has seen occupants; otherwise ask permission first.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r2.anchor: واختار الماوردي التفصيل وهو أنه إن وقعت عين المستأذن على من في البيت قبل دخوله قدم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r3.claim: Permission is most plainly requested by saying May I enter?; broader signals may qualify if they convey a request and alert the household.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن الإستئذان بما يدل على طلب الإذن صريحا والمأثور المشهور في ذلك أأدخل

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r4.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r4.claim: According to a report from Ata, asking permission is obligatory for every adult; the verse's apparent wording allows one woman to provide it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r4.anchor: وهو على ما لاوي عن عطاء واجب على كل محتلم ويكفي فيه المرأة الواحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r5.claim: Qatada describes three requests: the first alerts the household, the second lets them prepare, and the third leaves them free to admit or refuse.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r5.anchor: أخرج البيهقي في الشعب وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة أنه قال : كان يقال الإستئذان ثلاثا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r6.claim: A marfu report through Abu Sa'id says that if permission is not granted after three requests, the visitor should leave.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r6.anchor: وفي الأمر بالرجوع بعد الثلاث حديث مرفوع أخرجه مالك والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود عن أبي سعيد الخدري

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says not to exceed three requests unless it is established that the household did not hear them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r7.anchor: وذكر أبو حيان أنه لا يزيد على الثلاث إلا إن تحقق أن في البيت لم يسمع

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r8.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r8.claim: A man asked whether he had to ask permission before entering on his mother each time; the Prophet asked whether he wished to see her naked, then told him to ask.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r8.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أأستأذن على أمي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says people must ask permission before entering on their mothers and sisters.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير والبيهقي عن ابن مسعود عليكم أن تستأذنوا أمهاتكم وأخواتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r10.speaker: أم إياس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r10.claim: Umm Iyas recounts that Aisha initially refused entry to women until one greeted and asked permission, then invoked this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r10.anchor: عن أم إياس قالت : كنت في أربع نسوة نستأذن على عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r11.claim: The rule applies to women too; the masculine wording is inclusive, since householders may conceal private states from women as from men.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r11.anchor: وإذا صح ذلك ففي الآية نوع تغليب ووجه مشروعية الإستئذان لهن نحو وجه مشروعيته للرجال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r12.claim: Sound reports say permission was instituted because of looking, so one should not peer into a house before asking.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r12.anchor: وصح من حديث أخرجه الشيخان وغيرهما إنما جعل الإستئذان من أجل النظر ومن هنا لا ينبغي النظر في قعر البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r13.speaker: أبو أمامة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r13.claim: A report from the Prophet says a believer should not enter without permission and greeting; looking into a house counts as entry.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r13.anchor: وقد أخرج الطبراني عن أبي أمامة رضي الله تعالى عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن بشر
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r14.claim: Abd Allah b. Bishr reports that the Prophet stood beside a doorway rather than facing it and greeted occupants, since doors then had no curtains.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r14.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كما أخرج أبو داود والبخاري في الأدب المفرد عن عبد الله بن بشر إذا أتى باب قوم لم يستقبل الباب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r15.claim: The general address includes blind visitors, who may overhear private speech householders do not want them to hear.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135/r15.anchor: وظاهر الآية أيضا مشروعية الإستئذان للأعمى لدخوله في عموم الموصول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf says permission protects private conditions people ordinarily conceal from outsiders, not only against seeing nakedness; al-Alusi accepts it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r1.anchor: وفي الكشاف إنما شرع الإستئذان لئلا يوقف على الأحوال التي يطويها الناس في العادة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r2.claim: The hadith that permission is due to looking states the common reason, not an exclusive one; inna-ma can emphasize without restricting the rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r2.anchor: إنما جعل الإستئذان من أجل النظر خارج مخرج الغالب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r3.claim: Permission and greeting are distinct, though some reports treat permission as part of greeting; without greeting it is as nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r3.anchor: أن الإستئذان والتسليم متغايران لكن ظاهر بعض الأخبار يقتضي أن الإستئذان داخل في التسليم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim reports that Abd Allah's codex orders greeting the household and then asking permission.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r4.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله كما أخرج ابن جرير وغيره عن إبراهيم ( حتى تسلموا على أهلها

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r5.claim: One explanation takes that to refer to entering by the permission and greeting understood from the wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r5.anchor: إشارة على ما قيل إلى الدخول بالإستئذان والتسليم المفهوم من الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r6.claim: Another explanation takes that to refer directly to the two acts of seeking permission and greeting.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : إشارة إلى المذكور في ضمن الفعلين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r7.claim: The prescribed practice is better than sudden entry or pre-Islamic greetings; people sometimes entered and surprised a man with his wife under one blanket.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r7.anchor: من الدخول بغتة والدخول على تحية الجاهلية فقد كان الرجل منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r8.claim: One reading makes better reflect visitors' presumed feeling that waiting is humiliating; al-Alusi says the comparison needs no such assumption.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r8.anchor: خيرية المفضل عليه قيل على زعمهم لما في الأنتظار من المذلة ولعدم تحية الجاهلية حسنة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r9.claim: Khayr may simply function as an adjective, with no omitted comparative term understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r9.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ( خير ) صفة فلا تقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r10.claim: Some grammarians supply an omitted clause: you were guided to this so that you may remember, take heed, and act accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p135#2/r10.anchor: تعليل على ما اختاره جمع لمحذوف أي أرشدتم إلى ذلك أو قيل لكم هذا كي تتذكروا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ubayy read the phrase as until you ask permission; Ibn Abbas called the canonical wording a copyist's error.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r1.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقرأ حتى تستأذنوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r2.claim: The familiar reading تستأنسوا means asking permission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r2.anchor: والقراءة المعروفة تستأنسوا وهو بمعنى الاستئذان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r3.claim: Istī'nās can mean seeking familiarity: checking whether someone is home and telling the occupants one is entering.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: الاستئناس طلب الأنس، وهو أن ينظر هل في البيت إنسان فيؤذنهم إني داخل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r4.claim: Al-Khalil explains istī'nās as seeking to see clearly, from the phrase I saw a fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r4.anchor: وقال الخليل: الاستئناس الاستبصار من قوله: آنست نارا، أي: أبصرت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r5.claim: One may alert a household before entering by saying tasbīḥ or takbīr, or by clearing one's throat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو أن يتكلم بتسبيحة أو تكبيرة أو يتنحنح، يؤذن أهل البيت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r6.claim: One may not enter another's home until greeting its occupants and asking permission.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r6.anchor: أنه لا يدخل بيت الغير إلا بعد السلام والاستئذان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r7.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r7.claim: One group asks permission first, saying, May I enter? Peace be upon you.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r7.anchor: فقال قوم: يقدم الاستئذان فيقول: أأدخل سلام عليكم، لقوله تعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r8.speaker: الأكثرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r8.claim: Most greet first, then ask permission; they take the verse's order as reversed, as in Ibn Masud's codex.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r8.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه يقدم السلام فيقول: سلام عليكم أأدخل. وفي الآية تقديم وتأخير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r9.speaker: كلدة بن حنبل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r9.claim: After Kaldah entered without greeting or permission, the Prophet told him to return and say, Peace be upon you; may I enter?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن كلدة بن حنبل قال: دخلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم أسلم ولم أستأذن، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r10.claim: Ibn Umar refused a man's request to enter until someone prompted him to greet; after the greeting, he admitted him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r10.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أن رجلا استأذن عليه فقال: أأدخل؟ فقال ابن عمر: لا فأمر بعضهم الرجل أن يسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r11.claim: Some say to greet first when one sees someone inside; otherwise ask permission and then greet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إن وقع بصره على إنسان قدم السلام، وإلا قدم الاستئذان، ثم سلم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r12.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وحذيفة والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r12.claim: They require permission even to enter upon unmarriageable female relatives; in a shared home one should clear one's throat or move slightly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r12.anchor: وقال أبو موسى الأشعري وحذيفة: يستأذن على ذوات المحارم، ومثله عن الحسن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r13.claim: Abu Musa sought Umar's permission three times without reply and left; the Prophet's rule, reported by Abu Sa'id, was to leave after three unanswered greetings, which Umar required witnesses to establish.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p29#2/r13.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إذا سلم أحدكم ثلاثا فلم يجب فليرجع".

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r1.claim: The rule covers houses you do not inhabit; tenants and people using property on loan may not enter without permission either.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r1.anchor: التي لا تسكنونها فإن الآجر والمعير أيضا لا يدخلان إلا بإذن.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r2.claim: Seeking permission may mean seeking information about whether entry is wanted or permitted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r2.anchor: تستأذنوا من الاستئناس بمعنى الاستعلام من آنس الشيء إذا أبصره

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r3.claim: Alternatively, istiʾnās means becoming at ease after the visitor’s unease and fear of refusal are dispelled.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r3.anchor: أو من الاستئناس الذي هو خلاف الاستيحاش فإن المستأذن مستوحش خائف

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r4.claim: Alternatively, it means finding out whether anyone is inside.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r4.anchor: أو تتعرفوا هل ثم إنسان من الإنس.

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r5.claim: Greet the occupants by saying, “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r6.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r6.claim: The Prophet said to ask permission with the greeting three times; if permission is granted, enter, and otherwise return.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r6.anchor: التسليم أن يقول السلام عليكم أأدخل ثلاث مرات فإن أذن له دخل وإلا رجع

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r7.claim: “That is better” refers to permission or greeting rather than sudden entry, or is better than pre-Islamic greetings and abrupt entry that could expose a man and wife under one cover.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r7.anchor: أي الاستئذان أو التسليم خير لكم من أن تدخلوا بغتة، أو من تحية الجاهلية

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r8.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r8.claim: A man asked if he should seek permission to enter his mother’s room when she had no servant but him; the Prophet asked whether he would like to see her naked and told him to ask.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27/r8.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27-29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27-29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27-29/r1.claim: The phrase attaches to an omitted clause such as “this was revealed” or “this was said to you,” intending that you remember and act on what is best.
BAYDAWI-FULL:24:27-29/r1.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف أي أنزل عليكم، أو قيل لكم هذا إرادة أن تذكروا وتعملوا بما هو أصلح لكم.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r1.claim: The address describes people who have committed themselves to this religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r1.anchor: أيألزموا أنفسهم هذا الدين { لا تدخلوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r2.claim: Though the prohibition applies to each individual, it addresses the group because believers should restrain one another and prevent an individual from being overcome by Satan.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r2.anchor: فمن خان منهم منعه إخوانه , فلم يتكمن منه شيطانه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r3.claim: Other people's houses are houses in which the addressees do not reside.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r3.anchor: بيوتا غير بيوتكم } أي التي هي سكنكم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r4.claim: Seeking familiarity means asking permission so the occupants can feel at ease and the visitors can know them; answering only I does not identify the visitor, who should give a known name.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r4.anchor: أي تطلبوا بالاستئذان أن يأنس بكم من فيها وتأنسوا به , فلو قيل له : من ؟ فقال : أنا لم يحصل الاستئناس لعدم معرفته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r5.claim: Visitors should greet the residents, even temporary occupants, ask to enter, and knock if they may not hear the request.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r5.anchor: فتقولوا : السلام عليكم ! أأدخل ؟ أو تطرقوا الباب إن كان قد لا يسمع الاستئذان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r6.claim: Permission and greeting are better than entering unannounced or using pre-Islamic greetings: they spare visitors from seeing what they dislike, with greater benefit in the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r6.anchor: لأنكم إذا دخلتم بغير إذن ربما رأيتم ما يسوءكم , وإذا استأذنتم لم تدخلوا على ما تكرهون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r7.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r7.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reports that if a person greets three times and receives no answer, the person should return, provided the host is thought to have heard; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r7.anchor: وقد روى أبو موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه : إذا سلم ثلاثا فلم يجبه أحد فليرجع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r8.claim: The etiquette invites people to remember that they dislike others exposing their private circumstances, so they should treat others as they wish to be treated; recompense matches deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r8.anchor: فيعرف أن ما يسوءه غيره منه , فيفعل ما يحب أن يفعل معه خوفا من المقابلة , لأن الجزاء من جنس العمل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r9.claim: Practices required outside one's home are recommended at home too: make a throat-clearing or raise the voice in remembrance, following the warning against surprise night visits that might expose unwelcome sights.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p252/r9.anchor: وكل ما يجب عليه في غير بيته يستحب له في بيته بنحو النحنحة ورفع الصوت بالذكر ونحوه على ما أشار إليه حديث النهي عن الطروق

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r1.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r1.claim: A woman complained that relatives entered her home while she was in a state she did not want even her child or parent to see; this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r1.anchor: عن رجل من الأنصار قال: قالت: امرأة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إني أكون في بيتي

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the written wording a scribal error and says it should read hatta tasta'dhinū, until you ask permission.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها} قال: أخطأ الكاتب

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r3.claim: Ibrahim reports that Abdullah's codex placed greeting before asking permission.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال: في مصحف عبد الله (حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا)

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r4.claim: Ikrima reports that Ubayy's reading says to greet and then ask permission.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: هي في قراءة أبي (حتى تسلموا وتستأذنوا)

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains istinas as asking permission; he also summarizes istinas as istidhan.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {حتى تستأنسوا} قال: حتى تستأذنوا

DURR-FULL:v6p171/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r6.speaker: أبو أيوب
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r6.claim: Asked what istinas means, the Prophet says a man can announce himself with praise, takbir, tahmid or throat-clearing so the household is alerted.
DURR-FULL:v6p171/r6.anchor: عن أبي أيوب قال: قلت يا رسول الله أرأيت قول الله {حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا على أهلها} هذا التسليم قد عرفناه

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r1.speaker: أبو أيوب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r1.claim: The Prophet defines istinas as calling the servant so the household being greeted becomes aware of the visitor.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r1.anchor: عن أبي أيوب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الاستئناس أن تدعو الخادم حتى يستأنس أهل البيت

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses istinas as clearing one's throat and sniffing.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {حتى تستأنسوا} قال: تنحنحوا وتنخموا

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r3.speaker: رجل من بني عامر
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r3.claim: When a man asked the Prophet to enter, the Prophet sent a servant to teach him the proper formula: greeting, then asking to enter.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r3.anchor: رجل من بني عامر استأذن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بيت فقال: أألج فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r4.speaker: عمرو بن سعد الثقفي
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r4.claim: A man said a'alij to the Prophet; he told his servant Rawda to teach him to say peace be upon you, may I enter.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن سعد الثقفي أن رجلا استأذن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أألج فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r5.speaker: كلدة عن صفوان بن أمية
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r5.claim: Kilda entered the Prophet's presence without greeting or permission; the Prophet sent him back to greet and ask entry.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r5.anchor: من طريق كلدة أن صفوان بن أمية بعثه في الفتح بلياي وصقانيس والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأعلى الوادي

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Umar seeking entry by greeting the Messenger and asking whether Umar could enter.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: استأذن عمر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: السلام على رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r7.claim: Ibn Umar advises Zayd to greet first, then ask to enter; enter only if invited.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r7.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: أرسلني أبي إلى ابن عمر فجئته فقلت: أألج فقال: ادخل

DURR-FULL:v6p172/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r8.speaker: أم إياس
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r8.claim: Among four women seeking entry to Aisha, Umm Iyas asked if they should enter and Aisha said no.
DURR-FULL:v6p172/r8.anchor: عن أم إياس قالت: كنت في أربع نسوة نستأذن على عائشة فقلت: ندخل فقالت: لا

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r1.speaker: واحدة من النسوة
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r1.claim: In the continuation of Umm Iyas's report, a woman greets Aisha and asks to enter; Aisha lets them in and recites this verse.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r1.anchor: فقالت واحدة: السلام عليكم أندخل قالت: ادخلوا ثم قالت {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا بيوتا

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r2.claim: The Prophet says greeting should precede speech.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم السلام قبل الكلام

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra says a person who asks permission before greeting is not admitted until he begins with the greeting.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة فيمن يستأذن قبل أن يسلم قال: لا يؤذن له حتى يبدأ بالسلام

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra jokingly says that if someone enters without greeting, tell him no until he brings the key.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: إذا دخل ولم يقل السلام عليكم فقل: لا حتى تأتي بالمفتاح

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda says Abdullah would announce his arrival at home by speaking and raising his voice.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r5.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة قال: كان عبد الله إذا دخل الدار استأنس تكلم ورفع صوته

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r6.claim: Ibn Masud says one must seek permission before entering even on one's mothers and sisters.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: عليكم أن تستأذنوا على أمهاتكم وأخواتكم

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r7.claim: The Prophet says that when one's sight has entered, there is no permission for him.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا دخل البصر فلا اذن له

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r8.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r8.claim: The Prophet says that looking inside before asking permission and greeting disobeys God and gives no right of entry.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r8.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن الاستئذان في البيوت فقال من دخلت عينه

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r9.speaker: أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r9.claim: The Prophet says a believer must announce himself and greet before entering a home; looking into its interior counts as entering.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r9.anchor: عن أبي أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من كان يشهد أني رسول الله فلا يدخل على أهل بيت

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r10.speaker: هذيل
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r10.claim: The Prophet told Saad, who stood at the door, to move aside and explained that permission is required because of the risk of looking in.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r10.anchor: عن هذيل قال: جاء سعد فوقف على باب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستأذن فقام على الباب

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن بشر
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r11.claim: The Prophet stood to one side of a doorway rather than facing it, greeted twice, and did so because houses then had no curtains.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r11.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بشر قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتى باب قوم لم يستقبل الباب

DURR-FULL:v6p173/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r12.speaker: سهل بن سعد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r12.claim: When a man peered into the Prophet's room, the Prophet said he would have pierced his eye if he had known, explaining that permission protects privacy from sight.
DURR-FULL:v6p173/r12.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال: اطلع رجل من حجر في حجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعه مدرى يحك بها رأسه

DURR-FULL:v6p174/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r1.speaker: سهل بن سعد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r1.claim: An alternate wording of the Prophet's explanation says that God made permission because of sight.
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r1.anchor: وفي لفظ: إنما جعل الله الإذن من أجل البصر

DURR-FULL:v6p174/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r2.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r2.claim: The Prophet told Saad ibn Ubada to step away from the doorway and said permission exists to prevent looking in.
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن عبادة قال: جئت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بيته فقمت مقابل الباب فاستأذنت

DURR-FULL:v6p174/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r3.claim: Qatada equates istinas with asking permission and says it is done three times: first to be heard, second to alert the household, and third for them to decide whether to admit or refuse.
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {حتى تستأنسوا} قال: هو الاستئذان قال: وكان يقال الاستئذان ثلاث

DURR-FULL:v6p174/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r4.claim: Abu Musa left after three unanswered requests to enter, citing the Prophet's rule; Umar required a witness, and Abu Said testified, while Umar stressed the seriousness of reports from the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r4.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كنت جالسا في مجلس من مجالس الأنصار فجاء أبو موسى فزعا

DURR-FULL:v6p174/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says these are homes not belonging to the visitor; the order places greeting before permission-seeking, which is better than uninvited entry and lets residents prepare.
DURR-FULL:v6p174/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم} يعني بيوتا ليست لكم {حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا}

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains that these are houses that do not belong to the visitor.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r1.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r2.claim: Maqatil says pre-Islamic Arabs used casual morning or evening greetings and entered without leave, disturbing household privacy; God replaced this with permission and greeting to secure modesty and cleanliness.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r2.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان قوله : يا ايها الذين امنوا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda says Abdullah announced himself on entering a house by greeting and raising his voice.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r3.anchor: أبي عبيدة قال : كان عبد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses istiʾnās as asking permission to enter.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r4.anchor: ابن عباس قوله : لا تدخلوا بيوتا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, as related by Saʿid ibn Jubayr, says istiʾnās means asking permission and may be a scribal error in the written text.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r5.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قوله : حتى تستانسوا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r6.claim: Mujahid explains istiʾnās as clearing one's throat or spitting to signal presence.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r7.claim: Qatada prescribes seeking permission three times: announce yourself, allow the household to prepare, then accept either permission or refusal; if refused, leave without lingering at the door.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2565#2/r7.anchor: قتادة حتى تستانسوا قال : هو الاستئذان ثلاثا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says a visitor can announce himself with glorification, takbir, praise, or throat-clearing so the household knows he is there; no grading is stated.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r1.anchor: أبي ايوب قال : قلت يا رسول الله : هذا السلام

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r2.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains istiʾnās as the step before asking permission.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r2.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r3.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the phrase puts the actions in forward order: greet the household, then ask permission; greeting precedes the request.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r3.anchor: سعيد بن جبير قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r4.claim: Ikrima says that when entering an empty house one should say, Peace be upon us from our Lord, and peace be upon us and God's righteous servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r4.anchor: عكرمة في قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r5.claim: Maqatil says visitors should greet first, then ask permission so residents can prepare; they enter if admitted and return if told to do so.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r5.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان قوله : حتى تستانسوا وتسلموا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the better course is permission and greeting rather than entering without leave, avoiding sin and giving residents warning.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r6.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : ذلكم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr takes the reminder as the benefit of permission and greeting, by which one enters as God commanded.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2567/r7.anchor: سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : لعلكم تذكرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r1.claim: These rules advance the surah’s broader aim of regulating social and family dealings among neighbors, introducing visitation and permission etiquette so people follow a clear common procedure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r1.anchor: ذكرنا أن من أكبر الأغراض في هذه السورة تشريع نظام المعاشرة والمخالطة العائلية في التجاور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r2.claim: Permission was known in pre-Islamic times and early Islam but varied by the visitor’s status and could be skipped or abbreviated; these verses standardize it as religious etiquette.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r2.anchor: وقد كان الاستئذان معروفا في الجاهلية وصدر الإسلام ، وكان يختلف شكله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r3.claim: A visitor may be intent on satisfying an immediate need, while an unannounced or hurried entry can embarrass or burden the host; the prescribed etiquette guards against this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r3.anchor: وقد يتركه أو يقصر فيه من لا يهمه إلا قضاء وطره وتعجيل حاجته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r4.claim: Homes shelter people from heat, cold, rain, and dust, and protect private matters from unwanted exposure; a resident needs time to prepare or conceal them before admitting a visitor or speaking outside.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r4.anchor: وشرع الاستئذان لمن يزور أحدا في بيته لأن الناس اتخذوا البيوت للاستتار مما يؤذي الأبدان من حر وقر ومطر وقتام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r5.claim: Mālik, as transmitted by Ibn Wahb, takes tastaʾnisū as seeking permission, glossing it as seeking welcome or familiarity with the homeowner.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r5.anchor: قال ابن وهب قال مالك : الاستئناس فيما نرى والله أعلم الاستئذان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur endorses Mālik’s interpretation as decisive: the expression is a subtle metonymy for seeking permission, in a manner that will not make the householder uneasy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r6.anchor: وهذا كناية لطيفة عن الاستئذان ، أي أن يستأذن الداخل ، أي يطلب إذنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r7.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r7.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says istīnas means greeting; Ibn al-Arabi calls that remote, while Ibn Ashur explains it as greeting with the purpose of seeking permission, making the second clause explanatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r7.anchor: ووقع لابن القاسم في ( جامع العتيبة ) أن الاستئناس التسليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r8.claim: The word does not mean awareness or knowing here, a separate lexical use that does not fit the context or add a useful point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r8.anchor: وليس المراد بالاستئناس أنه مشتق من آنس بمعنى علم لأن ذلك إطلاق آخر لا يستقيم هنا فلا فائدة في ذكره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r9.claim: Permission indicates that the host does not dislike the visitor, while refusal signals displeasure; the wording thus alludes to the reason permission is required, although only God knows the host’s heart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p196/r9.anchor: فإنه إذا أذن له دل إذنه على أنه لا يكره دخوله وإذا كره دخوله لا يأذن له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r1.claim: Seeking permission is obligatory: it protects the person visited from unwelcome intrusion, dispute, insults, harsh speech, and grounds for suspicion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r1.anchor: فائدة الاستئذان دفع ما يكره عن المطروق المزور وقطع أسباب الإنكار أو الشتم أو الإغلاظ في القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r2.claim: Greeting alongside permission strengthens established affection; that purpose makes greeting emphatically recommended, not obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r2.anchor: فائدة السلام مع الاستئذان فهي تقوية الألفة المتقررة فلا تقتضي أكثر من تأكد الاستحباب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r3.claim: The Qur'an gives the complete form of proper conduct while the Sunnah explains its component rulings, as in the Qur'an's stated role of clarification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r3.anchor: فالقرآن أمر بالحالة الكاملة وأحال تفصيل أجزائها على تبيين السنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r4.claim: The verse summarizes the wisdom of permission: it brings benefit, which people are expected to recognize through reflection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r5.claim: The coordinating conjunction requires both courtesies but sets no order; either order fulfills the request, though reports prescribing greeting first make that order preferable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r5.anchor: جمعت الآية الاستئذان والسلام بواو العطف المفيد التشريك فقط فدلت على أنه إن قدم الاستئذان على السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r6.claim: Permission has no fixed formula; phrases found in reports reflect customary speech or a more concise way to express the purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r6.anchor: فإنما محمله على أنه المتعارف بينهم أو على أنه كلام أجمع من غيره في المراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r7.claim: A visitor who receives no permission repeats the request three times, then leaves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r7.anchor: أن المستأذن إن لم يؤذن له بالدخول يكرره ثلاث مرات فإذا لم يؤذن له انصرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r8.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari has Abu Musa cite the Prophet's rule to return after three unanswered requests; Umar asks for corroboration, Ubay sends the youngest witness, Abu Sa'id, and Umar says market business had distracted him from the report.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p198/r8.anchor: كنت في مجلس من مجالس الأنصار إذ جاء أبو موسى الأشعري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r1.speaker: عدي بن ثابت عن امرأة من الأنصار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r1.claim: An Ansari woman said male relatives sometimes entered while she was in a state she did not want even her father or child to see; the verse was revealed in response.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r1.anchor: سبب هذه الآية فيما ذكر الطبري بسند عن عدي بن ثابت أن امرأة من الأنصار قالت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r2.claim: The ruling applies to everyone permanently: one's private home is one occupied alone, with one's wife, or with one's slave woman; other homes are not one's own.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r2.anchor: ثم هي عامة في الأمة غابر الدهر من حيث هذه النازلة تختص بكل أحد في نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وغيره
