IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r3.claim: Ibn Masud and others say a person should seek permission before entering even his mother's home.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r3.anchor: قال ابن مسعود وغيره ينبغي للإنسان أن لا يدخل البيت الذي فيه أمه إلا بعد الاستيناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r4.claim: The Prophet tells a man who says his mother has no attendant but him to seek permission anyway, asking whether he would like to see her naked; the rule extends to every unmarriageable female relative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r4.anchor: وروي في ذلك حديث عن النبي عليه السلام أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله استأذن على أمي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r5.speaker: زينب امرأة ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r5.claim: Zaynab says Ibn Masud would clear his throat when arriving home so he would not surprise the household.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r5.anchor: وقالت زينب امرأة ابن مسعود كان ابن مسعود إذا جاء منزله تنحنح مخافة أن يهجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r6.claim: Tastaʾnisū means to inquire about and learn who is inside, perceiving them through the senses; the related verb can mean recognizing by sight or sound.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r6.anchor: وتستأنسوا معناه تستعملوا أي تستعلموا من في البيت وتستبصروا، تقول آنست إذا علمت عن حس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r7.speaker: حسان بن ثابت والحارث
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r7.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's line asks whether anyone can be discerned near al-Balqa, and al-Harith's line likewise uses the verb for sensing a sound at home.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r7.anchor: ومنه قول حسان بن ثابت «أنظر خليلي بباب جلق هل تؤنس دون البلقاء من أحد»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r8.claim: Ānasa follows the afʿala pattern and istaʾnasa the istifʿala pattern; the latter suggests seeking what puts both visitor and household at ease.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r8.anchor: ووزن آنس أفعل واستأنس وزنه استفعل فكأن المعنى في «تستأنسون» تطلبون ما يؤنسكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r9.claim: To learn the household's state, ask permission, clear one's throat, or otherwise announce oneself, then wait long enough for the occupants to prepare before entering.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r9.anchor: وإذا طلب الإنسان أن يعلم أمر البيت الذي يريد دخوله فذلك يكون بالاستئذان على من فيه أو بأن يتنحنح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r10.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r10.claim: Al-Tabari says it means making people inside aware of one's presence and ensuring oneself they have noticed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175/r10.anchor: وذهب الطبري في تستأنسوا إلى أنه بمعنى حتى تؤنسوا أهل البيت من أنفسكم بالتنحنح والاستئذان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the verb's morphology does not support deriving it from ānasa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.anchor: تصريف الفعل يأبى أن يكون من آنس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وأبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read tastaʾdhinū, as does Ubayy; Abu Hatim gives the order salimū then tastaʾdhinū, and Ibn Abbas is reported to call the written form an error.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ «حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا» وهي قراءة أبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya insists that all Muslim codices agree on tastaʾnisū since Uthman; the alternative reading is weak, and calling the agreed text erroneous cannot credibly be attributed to Ibn Abbas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.anchor: مصاحف الإسلام كلها قد ثبت فيها تستأنسوا وصح الإجماع فيها من لدن مدة عثمان رضي الله عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.claim: He considers tastaʾdhinū a gloss rather than a reading, since Ibn Abbas also explains tastaʾnisū as seeking permission and the wording is clear Arabic.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.claim: Umar's request to the Prophet at the chamber door shows that the word can mean seeking company or welcome, making Ibn Abbas's alleged rejection implausible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.anchor: وقد قال عمر للنبي عليه السلام: استأنس يا رسول الله وعمر واقف على باب الغرفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.claim: These authorities say the clause allowing entry to uninhabited houses abrogates or exempts the first verse; Ibn Atiyya rejects this because the verses concern inhabited and public uninhabited houses, respectively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.anchor: وحكى الطبري أيضا بسند عن ابن جريج عن ابن عباس وعكرمة والحسن بن أبي الحسن أنهم قالوا نسخ واستثني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.claim: Greet the occupants and ask to enter; enter if invited, leave if told to return, and depart after three unanswered requests.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.anchor: وصورة الاستئذان أن يقول الرجل السلام عليكم أأدخل؟ فإن أذن له دخل وإن أمر بالرجوع انصرف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.claim: A man at the Prophet's house asks whether to enter; the Prophet has his servant Rawda teach him the greeting and request, then grants entry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.anchor: فروى الطبري أن رجلا جاء إلى بيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال آلج أو أنلج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.claim: When Ibn Umar asks to enter a woman's tent, she says enter with peace; he explains that this could mean enter with one's greeting rather than one's person, and asks her to say simply enter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.anchor: وروي أن ابن عمر آذته الرمضاء يوما فأتى فسطاط امرأة من قريش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.claim: Communities may use their own customary wording when asking permission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.anchor: ثم لكل قوم في الاستئذان عرفهم في العبارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وأبو سعيد الخدري وأبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.claim: The rule to return after three requests is established by the report of Abu Musa with Umar, witnessed for Abu Musa by Abu Said and Ubayy ibn Kab.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.anchor: وأما ثبوت الرجوع بعد الاستئذان ثلاثا فلحديث أبي موسى الأشعري الذي استعمله مع عمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r12.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r12.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says permission is obligatory for everyone who has reached puberty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r12.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح الاستئذان واجب على كل محتلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r13.claim: The Prophet says a man's messenger counts as his permission to enter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r13.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «رسول الرجل إذنه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r14.claim: That is better for you closes the sentence; the reminder means God instructed people in this way to prompt reflection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p175#2/r14.anchor: وقوله: ذلكم خير لكم تم الكلام عنده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r1.claim: These are divinely taught manners: seek permission before entering another's home, then greet its occupants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r1.anchor: أي: يستأذنوا قبل الدخول ويسلموا بعده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r2.claim: The visitor should ask permission three times and leave if no permission is given.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r2.anchor: وينبغي أن يستأذن ثلاثا، فإن أذن له، وإلا انصرف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r3.claim: After Abū Mūsā left when ʿUmar did not answer his three requests, ʿUmar demanded proof; Abū Saʿīd testified, and ʿUmar said market business had distracted him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r3.anchor: أن أبا موسى حين استأذن على عمر ثلاثا، فلم يؤذن له، انصرف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r4.speaker: أنس (أو غيره)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r4.claim: In a report attributed uncertainly to Anas, the Prophet greeted Saʿd three times; Saʿd answered quietly to gain more greetings and blessings, then hosted him and received a prayer of blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p36/r4.anchor: عن أنس -أو: غيره (4) أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استأذن على سعد بن عبادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr says the Saʿd visit report also comes by another route and considers it a good, strong hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r1.anchor: فهو حديث جيد قوي، والله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r2.claim: The Prophet approached a household from the right or left side of its door, not directly in front, and greeted them; the houses then had no curtains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بسر (3) قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتى باب قوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r3.speaker: سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r3.claim: When a man stood facing the Prophet's door to ask entry, the Prophet told him to move aside, explaining that permission protects against looking in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r3.anchor: جاء رجل -قال عثمان: سعد -فوقف على باب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يستأذن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r4.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet says there is no blame if someone who peeks without permission is struck with a pebble that blinds him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r4.anchor: لو أن امرأ اطلع عليك بغير إذن فخذفته بحصاة، ففقأت عينه، ما كان عليك من جناح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r5.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r5.claim: Jābir knocked over a debt owed by his father; when he answered the Prophet's question with only “I,” the Prophet repeated the word as if disliking the vague identification.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r5.anchor: عن جابر قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دين كان على أبي، فدققت الباب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r6.claim: Saying “I” does not identify a visitor; he should state his name or familiar byname, so the purpose of permission seeking can be met.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37/r6.anchor: لأن هذه اللفظة لا يعرف صاحبها حتى يفصح باسمه أو كنيته التي هو مشهور بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and other authorities explain istīnā as asking permission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: الاستئناس: الاستئذان. وكذا قال غير واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly called the written wording a scribal error and read “until you ask permission and greet,” following Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية: {لا تدخلوا بيوتا غير بيوتكم حتى تستأنسوا وتسلموا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm reports that Ibn Masʿūd's codex said “greet the household and ask permission”; the same reading is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.anchor: وقال هشيم (2) أخبرنا مغيرة، عن إبراهيم قال: في مصحف ابن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarīr chooses the wording attributed to Ibn Masʿūd, which places greeting before seeking permission.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.anchor: وهذا أيضا رواية عن ابن عباس، وهو اختيار ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.speaker: كلدة بن الحنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.claim: Kalda entered without greeting or permission while bringing provisions sent by Ṣafwān; after Ṣafwān had converted, the Prophet sent him back to greet and ask entry. Al-Tirmidhī calls it ḥasan gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.anchor: أن صفوان بن أمية بعثه في الفتح بلبأ وجداية وضغابيس، والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأعلى الوادي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r6.speaker: رجل من بني عامر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r6.claim: The Prophet taught a visitor who asked simply “May I enter?” to say “Peace be upon you; may I enter?”; the man repeated it and was admitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p37#2/r6.anchor: عن منصور، عن ربعي قال: حدثنا (4) رجل من بني عامر استأذن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r1.speaker: رجل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r1.claim: In a report through Ibn Sīrīn and ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, the Prophet has his servant Rawḍa teach a visitor to greet and ask entry; he repeats it and is admitted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r1.anchor: أن رجلا استأذن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أألج -أو: أنلج؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r2.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet's saying that greeting comes before speech; al-Tirmidhī calls ʿAnbasa weak and abandoned and Muḥammad ibn Zādhān munkar in hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r2.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "السلام قبل الكلام"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r3.claim: Mujāhid recounts Ibn ʿUmar asking a Qurashī woman permission with greetings; after repeated replies, he prompts her to say “enter,” and goes in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: جاء ابن عمر من حاجة، وقد آذاه الرمضاء، فأتى فسطاط امرأة من قريش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r4.speaker: أم إياس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r4.claim: Um Iyas says that when several women asked to enter ʿĀʾisha's home, ʿĀʾisha told them to greet and ask permission, then admitted them and cited the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r4.anchor: حدثتني جدتي أم إياس قالت: كنت في أربع نسوة نستأذن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says people must seek permission even when entering upon their mothers and sisters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r5.anchor: عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود قال: عليكم أن تستأذنوا على أمهاتكم وأخواتكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r6.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r6.claim: An Anṣārī woman said male relatives entered while she was in a private state, even when she did not wish her father or son to see her; the verse was revealed in response.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p38/r6.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت: إن امرأة من الأنصار قالت: يا رسول الله، إني أكون في منزلي على الحال التي لا أحب أن يراني أحد عليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people deny the rule of seeking permission, as they deny that nobility before God is measured by piety rather than having the grandest house.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضي الله عنه، قال: ثلاث آيات جحدها الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās refuses to excuse a man from seeking permission to enter on orphan sisters living with him, asking whether he would want to see them unclothed and whether he wants to obey God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r2.anchor: أستأذن على أخواتي أيتام في حجري، معي في بيت واحد؟ قال: نعم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r3.speaker: طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r3.claim: Ṭāwūs says he would strongly dislike seeing a close female relative unclothed and was strict about the matter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r3.anchor: ابن طاوس عن أبيه قال: ما من امرأة أكره إلي أن أرى عريتها من ذات محرم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says permission must be sought even on one's mothers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r4.anchor: سمعت هزيل بن شرحبيل الأودي الأعمى، أنه سمع ابن مسعود يقول: عليكم الإذن على أمهاتكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says a man need not ask permission to enter on his wife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r5.anchor: قلت لعطاء: أيستأذن الرجل على امرأته؟ قال: لا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr understands ʿAṭāʾ to deny obligation only; it is still better to announce one's arrival to avoid surprising one's wife when she may be improperly dressed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r6.anchor: وهذا محمول على عدم الوجوب، وإلا فالأولى أن يعلمها بدخوله ولا يفاجئها به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r7.speaker: زينب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r7.claim: Zaynab, wife of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, says that when he reached the door he cleared his throat and spat so he would not surprise them; Ibn Kathīr calls the chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r7.anchor: عن زينب، رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان عبد الله إذا جاء من حاجة فانتهى إلى الباب، تنحنح وبزق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r8.speaker: أبو هبيرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r8.claim: Abū Hubayra says ʿAbd Allāh would announce himself when entering the house by speaking and raising his voice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r8.anchor: عن أبي هبيرة (1) قال: كان عبد الله إذا دخل الدار استأنس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r9.claim: Mujāhid explains “seek familiarity” as clearing the throat or spitting.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r10.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r10.claim: Aḥmad considers it recommended for a man entering his own home to clear his throat or move his sandals to alert its occupants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p39/r10.anchor: عن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل، رحمه الله، أنه قال: إذا دخل الرجل بيته، استحب له أن يتنحنح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r1.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet forbids a man from arriving at his family's home at night to surprise or spy on them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r1.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه نهى أن يطرق الرجل أهله طروقا -وفي رواية: ليلا يتخونهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r2.claim: When the Prophet reached Medina by day, he told the party to wait until evening before entering, allowing an unkempt woman to comb her hair and an absent woman's pubic hair to be trimmed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة نهارا، فأناخ بظاهرها، وقال: "انتظروا حتى تدخل عشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r3.speaker: أبو أيوب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r3.claim: Asked what istīnā means beyond greeting, the Prophet says to say tasbīḥ, takbīr, and taḥmīd or clear one's throat to alert the household; Ibn Kathīr calls the report gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r3.anchor: عن أبي أيوب قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، هذا السلام، فما الاستئناس؟ قال: "يتكلم الرجل بتسبيحة وتكبيرة وتحميدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r4.claim: Qatāda equates istīnā with seeking permission: ask three times to alert the household, give them time to prepare, and allow them to accept or refuse; if refused, do not linger at the door.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {حتى تستأنسوا} قال: هو الاستئذان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r5.claim: Muqātil recounts that pre-Islamic Arabs used morning or evening greetings, entered friends' houses without permission, and announced themselves, distressing households; God replaced this with privacy, chastity, and purity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان في قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تدخلوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr endorses Muqātil's account and explains that seeking permission is better for both visitor and household, so people may remember.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p40/r6.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله مقاتل حسن؛ ولهذا قال: {ذلكم خير لكم} يعني: الاستئذان خير لكم

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والأعمش
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r1.claim: They read تستأذنوا; the meaning is the same or an explanatory gloss for تستأنسوا.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والأعمش: (تستأذنوا)، والمعنى واحد، ويحتمل أنهم فسروا ذلك بقولهم: تستأذنوا

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r2.claim: The attribution to Ibn ʿAbbas that this was a copyist’s error is unsound; it would be a grave error Muslims could not all have accepted.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r2.anchor: قلنا: لا يصح ذلك عنه، وذلك غلط عظيم؛ لأنه لو كان كذلك لما جوزه الصحابة والتابعون والمسلمون إلى يومنا هذا

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r5.claim: Anistu can mean knew, saw, or heard; istīnās is seeking familiarity through knowledge.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r5.anchor: والاستئناس استفعال منه، وقيل: تستأنسوا أي: تنظروا هل هاهنا أحد يأذن

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r6.speaker: ابن عروة
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUrwa explains تستأنسوا as looking to see whether anyone is there to grant permission.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r6.anchor: وقيل: تستأنسوا أي: تنظروا هل هاهنا أحد يأذن، عن ابن عروة

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r7.claim: Another explanation equates تستأنسوا with تستأذنوا: asking whether entry is permitted.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه تستأذنوا. والاستئذان: الاستعلام، أي: استعلموا أيطلق لكم الدخول أم لا

JISHUMI:v7p5164/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r8.speaker: عبد الله
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r8.claim: A report says ʿAbd Allah would announce himself and speak when entering his home.
JISHUMI:v7p5164/r8.anchor: ومنه حديث عبد الله: (كان إذا دخل داوه استأنس وتكلم)

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r1.speaker: امرأة من الأنصار
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r1.claim: An Anṣārī woman said male relatives entered her home while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the permission verse was revealed.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r1.anchor: وقيل: روي أن امرأة من الأنصار جاءت إلى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وعلى آله، وقالت: يا رسول الله، إني أكون في منزلي على حال لا أحب أن يراني عليها أحد

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r3.claim: The permission rule follows the slander account because suspicion arose from seclusion; asking leave and greeting keeps people farther from accusation.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r3.anchor: لما كان ذلك لتهمة الخلوة، أمر الله تعالى عباده أن يتجنبوا مواضع التهم، وألا يدخلوا بيوتا حتى يستأنسوا ويسلموا على أهلها

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r4.claim: Another link is to the prior statement that God purifies whom He wills: permission-seeking is among purification.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r4.anchor: وقيل: لما تقدم قوله: (ولكن الله يزكي من يشاء) بين أن من جملة التطهير الاستئذان

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وإبراهيم وقتادة
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r13.claim: These authorities explain تستأنسوا as seeking permission.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r13.anchor: قيل: تستأذنوا، عن ابن عباس، وابن مسعود، وإبراهيم، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r14.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r14.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddī explain it as clearing the throat or speaking to serve as asking permission.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r14.anchor: وقيل: تستأنسوا بالتنحنح والكلام الذي يقوم مقام الاستئذان، عن مجاهد، والسدي

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r15.speaker: أبو موسى
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r15.claim: Abu Musa reports from the Prophet that permission is requested three times, then one returns if not admitted; ʿUmar demanded proof and Abu Musa brought a witness.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r15.anchor: وذكر الحسن أن أبا موسى روى عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: الاستئذان ثلاث، فإذا أذنوا وإلا فارجع، فدعاه عمر وقال: لتأتين ببينة، أو لأعاقبنك

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r16.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r16.claim: ʿIkrima takes seeking familiarity to mean saying tasbīḥ, takbīr, or similar words.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r16.anchor: وقيل: هو التسبيح والتكبير ونحوه، عن عكرمة

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r17.claim: A report tells of a man clearing his throat at the Prophet’s door; the Prophet had a woman teach him to say Peace be upon you, may I enter?, then admitted him.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r17.anchor: وروي أنه استأذن رجل على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وعلى آله فتنحنح فقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لامرأة: قومي إليه فعلميه فقولي له: قل: السلام عليكم، أأدخل؟

JISHUMI:v7p5166/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r18.speaker: ابن الأنباري
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r18.claim: Ibn al-Anbari explains istīnās as seeking guidance or finding company, as in the phrase about perceiving a fire.
JISHUMI:v7p5166/r18.anchor: وقيل: الاستئناس: الاستهداء، ومعناه حتى تجدوا أنيسا، عن ابن الأنباري من قوله: (آنست نارا)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r1.claim: One sense of tastaʾnisū is becoming at ease after the uncertainty of knocking at another's door; the phrase means waiting until permission is given.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه من الاستئناس الظاهر الذي هو خلاف الاستيحاش لأن الذي يطرق باب غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r2.claim: This is an indirect, consequent expression for permission, as in the rule against entering the Prophet's houses unless admitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r2.anchor: فالمعنى : حتى يؤذن لكم كقوله : { لا تدخلوا بيوت النبى إلا أن يؤذن لكم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r3.claim: This is a kināya and iridāf: the ease of knowing one's status follows permission, so the expression is put in its place.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r3.anchor: وهذا من باب الكناية والإرداف ؛ لأن هذا النوع من الاستئناس يردف الإذن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r4.claim: A second sense is to inquire or investigate whether entry is wanted, from seeing something plainly; al-Nābigha's “on one observant of solitude” illustrates the usage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r4.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون من الاستئناس الذي هو الاستعلام والاستكشاف : استفعال من أنس الشيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r5.claim: Common expressions such as “look whether you see anyone” and “I looked and saw no one” mean that the speaker sought information; al-Nābigha's مستأنس is cited for the sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r5.anchor: ومنه قولهم : استأنس هل ترى أحدا ، واستأنست فلم أر أحدا ، أي : تعرفت واستعلمت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r6.claim: It may instead derive from al-ins, meaning to find out whether a person is present.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من الإنس ، وهو أن يتعرف هل ثمة إنسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r7.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r7.claim: Asked what istī'nās means, the Prophet answered that a man says tasbīḥ, takbīr, or taḥmīd and clears his throat to alert the household.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r7.anchor: وعن أبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنه : قلنا : يا رسول الله ، ما الاستئناس ؟ قال : يتكلم الرجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r8.claim: The visitor should greet the household, ask “may I enter?” and repeat this three times; if permission is not granted, he returns.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r8.anchor: والتسليم أن يقول : السلام عليكم ، أأدخل ؟ ثلاث مرات ؛ فإن أذن له وإلا رجع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r9.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r9.claim: Abū Mūsā came to ʿUmar's door, requested entry three times, then left, citing the Prophet's rule that permission is sought three times.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r9.anchor: ( 742 ) وعن أبي موسى الأشعري أنه أتى باب عمر رضي الله عنهما فقال : السلام عليكم أأدخل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r10.claim: A man asked to enter by saying “May I come in?”; the Prophet had Rawḍa teach him the proper greeting and request, then admitted him when he used it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r10.anchor: ( 743 ) واستأذن رجل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : أألج ؟ فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لامرأة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r11.claim: Pre-Islamic visitors entered others' homes after a morning or evening greeting without asking, sometimes surprising a couple together; God stopped this and taught a better, more decent practice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r11.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يقول الرجل منهم إذا دخل بيتا غير بيته : حييتم صباحا ، وحييتم مساء ، ثم يدخل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r12.claim: People have abandoned this religious etiquette like a superseded custom, even when they know the revelation and Prophetic teaching; the author rebukes inattentive listeners.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r12.anchor: وكم من باب من أبواب الدين هو عند الناس كالشريعة المنسوخة قد تركوا العمل به ، وباب الاستئذان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r13.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r13.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading reverses the order: “until you greet the household and ask permission.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r13.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : ( حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say the wording was tastaʾdhِنū and the scribe erred; al-Zamakhsharī rejects this report as unreliable.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r14.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير : إنما هو حتى تستأذنوا ، فأخطأ الكاتب . ولا يعول على هذه الرواية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r15.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r15.claim: Ubayy also reads “until you ask permission.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r15.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي : ( حتى تستأذنوا ) { ذالكم } الاستئذان والتسليم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r16.claim: Dhālikum refers jointly to asking permission and greeting the residents.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r16.anchor: { ذالكم } الاستئذان والتسليم { خير لكم } من تحية الجاهلية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r17.claim: Al-dumūr is entering without leave; its derivation from al-damār (destruction) likens the offender to someone doomed because of the gravity of the act.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p230/r17.anchor: والدمور وهو الدخول بغير إذن واشتقاقه من الدمار وهو الهلاك ، كأن صاحبه دامر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the scribe erred by writing tastaʾnisū rather than tastaʾdhinū, and that he recited the latter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : أخطأ الكاتب فيه فكتب تستأنسوا وكان يقرأ : حتى تستأذنوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r2.speaker: غيره
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r2.claim: Another view takes the word as seeking permission because asking permission makes the household feel at ease; it alleges no scribal or recitational error.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r2.anchor: وقال غيره : لأن الاستئذان مؤنس فعبر عنه بالاستئناس , وليس فيه خطأ من كاتب

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r3.claim: Mujahid explains the phrase as making the household aware of the visitor by clearing the throat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r3.anchor: الثاني : معناه حتى تؤنسوا أهل البيت بالتنحنح فيعلموا بقدومك عليهم , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba takes it to mean finding out whether anyone is home, then asking permission and greeting them; he links the verb to 4:6, where it means knowing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r4.anchor: الثالث : أن تستأنسوا يعني أن تعلموا فيها أحدا استأذنوه فتسلموا عليه ومنه قوله تعالى : ^ { فإن آنستم منهم رشدا }

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says istinas means seeking or soliciting, while inas means certainty.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي الاستئناس الاستثمار ، والإيناس اليقين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r6.claim: Permission may be conveyed verbally or by gesture; a caller's loud request counts as asking.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r6.anchor: والإذن يكون بالقول والإشارة . فإن جاهر فسؤال , فقد روى قتادة عن أبي هريرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's rule that a man's messenger serves as his permission and that one who is not admitted after asking three times should leave without asking again.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r7.anchor: فقد روى قتادة عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( رسول الرجل إذنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r8.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Abu Musa sought entry to ʿUmar three times, left when unanswered, and cited the Prophet's rule; ʿUmar demanded proof, and Talha testified for him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r8.anchor: روى الحسن البصري أن [ أبا موسى ] الأشعري استأذن على عمر رضي الله عنه ثلاثا فلم يؤذن له فرجع

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r9.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r9.claim: Al-Hasan classifies the three requests as the first permission, the second consultation, and the third decisive notice, after which the household can admit or refuse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r9.anchor: قال الحسن : الأولى إذن , والثانية مؤامرة , والثالثة : عزمة , إن شاءوا أذنوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r10.claim: A visitor should not face the door when it is open, permission given to the first in a group covers the last, and a refused visitor should not sit at the door because people have needs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r10.anchor: ولا يستأذن وهو مستقبل الباب إن كان مفتوحا ، وإن أذن لأول القوم فقد أذن لآخرهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r11.claim: Greeting the household is recommended, whereas seeking permission is obligatory.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r12.claim: One view makes greeting a recommended act after permission, following the verse's order.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r12.anchor: { وتسلموا على أهلها } والسلام ندب والاستئذان حتم . وفي السلام قولان : أحدهما : أنه مسنون بعد الإذن

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r13.claim: Another view recommends greeting before permission; although greeting comes later in the recitation, it comes first in the legal ordering.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p85/r13.anchor: الثاني : مسنون قبل الإذن وإن تأخر في التلاوة فهو مقدم في الحكم وتقدير الكلام حتى تسلموا

MUJAHID:v2p439/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p439/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p439/r1.claim: Mujahid explains seeking permission as clearing one's throat or spitting to announce oneself.
MUJAHID:v2p439/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ حتى تستأنسوا ﴾ يعني تتنحنحوا تتنخموا

MUQATIL:24:27-29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r2.claim: The order implies greeting first and asking permission afterward.
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r2.anchor: فيها تقديم فابدءوا بالسلام قبل الاستئذان

MUQATIL:24:27-29/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r3.claim: Before this verse, people greeted one another in pre-Islamic fashion with “Good morning and evening”; the verse institutes greeting and permission.
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r3.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا فى الجاهلية يقول بعضهم لبعض: حييت صباحا ومساء، فهذه كانت تحية القوم بينهم

MUQATIL:24:27-29/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r4.claim: Greeting and asking permission are better than entering without leave, and allow the household to be ready.
MUQATIL:24:27-29/r4.anchor: يعنى السلام والاستئذان { خير لكم } يعنى أفضل لكم من أن تدخلوا بغير إذن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r1.claim: These are houses that you neither own nor inhabit.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r1.anchor: أى بيوتا لستم تملكونها ولا تسكنونها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses tastaʾnisū as asking permission and read it that way.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r2.anchor: أى تستأذنوا عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وقد قرأبه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r3.claim: Istī'nās originally means seeking information or discovering something; the verb derives from seeing something clearly and exposed, and here means finding out whether entry is permitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r3.anchor: والاستئناس فى الأصل الاستعلام واستكشاف استفعال من أنس الشئ إذا أبصره ظاهرا مكشوفا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r4.claim: Permission may be sought by saying a tasbīḥ, takbīr, taḥmīd, or by clearing one's throat.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r4.anchor: وذلك بتسبيحة أو بتكبيرة أو بتحميدة أو بتنحنح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r5.claim: The greeting is to say “Peace be upon you”; ask to enter three times, and if permission is not given, return.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r5.anchor: والتسليم أن يقول السلام عليكم أأدخل ثلاث مرات فإن أذن له والا رجع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r6.claim: Another view says to offer the greeting first when visitor and host meet; otherwise ask permission first.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r6.anchor: وقيل إن تلاقيا يقدم التسليم والا فالاستئذان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r7.claim: Permission and greeting are better than the pre-Islamic greeting and al-dumūr, entering without leave; people used to greet and walk in, sometimes finding a man with his wife under one blanket.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r7.anchor: والدمور وهو الدخول بغير إذن فكان الرجل من أهل الجاهلية إذا دخل بيت غيره يقول حييتم صباحا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r8.claim: Dhālikum refers to asking permission and offering the greeting.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r9.claim: The instruction is given so people remember, take heed, and practice the rules of asking permission.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p142/r9.anchor: أى قيل لكم هذا لكى تذكروا وتتعظوا وتعملوا ما أمرتم به فى باب الاستئذان

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r1.claim: God gave people homes for privacy and private enjoyment, forbade outsiders from looking in or entering without permission, and protected their seclusion and modesty.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r1.anchor: وحجر على الخلق أن يطلعوا على ما فيها من خارج أو يلجوها من غير إذن أربابها

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r2.claim: Muslim reports from Abū Hurayra that a person who looks into a home without permission may have his eye gouged out.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r3.claim: Some scholars say the eye-gouging report is not literal: the gouger would owe compensation and the report was abrogated by 16:126.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r3.anchor: فقال بعض العلماء: ليس هذا على ظاهره

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r4.claim: Another possibility treats the threat as a warning, not a binding rule; a report contradicting the Qurʾān cannot be acted upon.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون خارج على وجه الوعيد لا على وجه الحتم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r5.claim: The Prophet’s reported order to Bilāl to “cut” ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās’s tongue after praise meant to give him something, not literally cut it.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r5.anchor: لما مدحه قال لبلال: «قم فاقطع لسانه» وإنما أراد بذلك أن يدفع إليه شيئا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r6.claim: The threat may figuratively mean imposing a consequence that prevents the intruder from looking into another home again.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r6.anchor: وكذلك هذا يحتمل أن يكون ذكر فقء العين والمراد أن يعمل به عمل حتى لا ينظر بعد ذلك في بيت غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r7.claim: Qurtubi’s preferred ruling is that the person who gouges the intruder’s eye owes neither compensation nor retaliation, relying on a report from Anas cited later.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لا ضمان عليه ولا قصاص وهو الصحيح إن شاء الله تعالى لحديث أنس

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r8.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r8.claim: A report from ʿAdī ibn Thābit says an Anṣārī woman asked how to prevent male relatives entering while she was in a state she did not want seen; the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r8.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت أن امرأة من الأنصار قالت:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r9.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27/r9.claim: Abū Bakr asked about unoccupied inns and roadside dwellings in Syria; 24:29 was then revealed to exempt uninhabited homes.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r1.claim: Malik, as quoted by Ibn Wahb, says tastaʾnisū means seek permission; this wording is also attributed as a reading to Ubayy, Ibn Abbas, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن وهب قال مالك: الاستئناس فيما نرى والله أعلم الاستئذان

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the word as finding out who is home; Mujahid says to clear the throat or otherwise signal, wait until noticed, then enter.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: بالتنحنح أو بأي وجه أمكن

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r3.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī gives the sense of learning who is inside and supports it with 4:6, where ānastum means “you know.”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r3.anchor: وقال معناه الطبري ومنه قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r4.speaker: أبو أيوب الأنصاري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r4.claim: A report in Ibn Mājah from Abū Ayyūb says the Prophet defined istī’nās as speaking a tasbīḥ, takbīr, or taḥmīd, clearing one’s throat, and notifying the household.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r5.claim: Qurtubi says the Abū Ayyūb report plainly makes istī’nās distinct from asking permission, agreeing with Mujahid and those who share his view.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r5.anchor: وهذا نص في أن الاستئناس غير الاستئذان كما قال مجاهد ومن وافقه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r6.claim: A claim attributed to Ibn Abbas and others calls tastaʾnisū a scribal error for tastaʾdhinū; Qurtubi rejects this because the codices and Companion consensus preserve the received wording since ʿUthmān’s era.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وبعض الناس يقول عن سعيد بن جبير

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r7.claim: Qurtubi invokes 41:42 and 15:9 to argue the received Qurʾānic wording cannot be corrupted and the Companions’ agreed codices cannot be called erroneous.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Abū Ḥātim, proposes fronting and delaying: greet the household and then seek their notice.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r8.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that rearrangement: tastaʾnisū is clear Arabic, and Umar used it while standing at the Prophet’s room.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r9.anchor: ابن عطية: ومما ينفي هذا القول عن ابن عباس وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r10.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r10.claim: A well-known report has Umar at the Prophet’s room asking permission with the phrase astaʾnis, “May I seek your notice?”
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r10.anchor: وقد قال عمر للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أستأنس يا رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r11.claim: From the Abū Ayyūb report, Qurtubi concludes istī’nās precedes the greeting, so the verse remains in its stated order without transposition.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r11.anchor: قد ذكرنا من حديث أبي أيوب أن الاستئناس إنما يكون قبل السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r12.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r12.claim: The Sunnah is to ask permission three times and not exceed that; Malik allows another try only when certain the occupants did not hear.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r12.anchor: قال ابن وهب قال مالك: الاستئذان ثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r13.claim: The visitor should greet and ask to enter, enter if allowed, leave if told to return, and depart after three unanswered requests.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r13.anchor: السلام عليكم أأدخل فإن أذن له دخل

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r14.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#2/r14.claim: In the famous authentic report, Abū Mūsā told Umar he had greeted three times at his door without response and left; the Prophet instructed that an unanswered third request requires returning.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r1.claim: Three repetitions usually ensure speech is heard and understood; the Prophet repeated statements for comprehension and greeted people three times.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r1.anchor: إنما خص الاستئذان بثلاث لأن الغالب من الكلام إذا كرر ثلاثا سمع وفهم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r2.claim: After three unanswered requests the host likely refuses or cannot answer; the visitor should leave rather than disturb or harm the host by insisting.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r2.anchor: فإذا لم يؤذن له بعد ثلاث ظهر أن رب المنزل لا يريد الإذن

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r3.speaker: أبو أيوب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r3.claim: Qurtubi cites the Prophet telling Abū Ayyūb, who hurried out after seeking permission, “Perhaps we made you hurry,” illustrating the burden of insistence.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي أيوب حين استأذن عليه فخرج مستعجلا

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r4.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r4.claim: Ibn Shihāb narrates that the Prophet greeted Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda three times and left without reply; Saʿd had heard and wanted more greetings, so he caught up and explained.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#3/r4.anchor: وروى عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أما سنة التسليمات الثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r1.speaker: ابن شهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r1.claim: Ibn Shihāb says the three greetings derive from the Saʿd incident; another Abū Dāwūd transmission includes Qays ibn Saʿd, while other transmitters give it mursal without Qays.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن شهاب: فإنما أخذ التسليم ثلاثا من قبل ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have said people abandoned asking permission; scholars suggest this followed the widespread use of doors and knocking.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r2.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الاستئذان ترك العمل به الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r3.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr that the Prophet stood to a doorway’s right or left, not directly in front, and called out the greeting twice because homes then had no curtains.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r3.anchor: روى أبو داود عن عبد الله بن بسر

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r4.claim: At a closed door one may stand where convenient and seek permission, or knock.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r4.anchor: فإن كان الباب مردودا فله أن يقف حيث شاء منه ويستأذن

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r5.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r5.claim: A report from Abū Mūsā says the Prophet was at a garden well when Abū Bakr knocked and was admitted with glad tidings of Paradise; Qurtubi judges the chain through ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nāfiʿ sounder than al-Laythī’s variant.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r5.anchor: أبو موسى الأشعري: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في حائط بالمدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r6.claim: Knocking should be gentle enough to be heard and not forceful; Anas reports that the Prophet’s doors were tapped with fingernails.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r6.anchor: وصفة الدق أن يكون خفيفا بحيث يسمع

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r7.claim: In both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet asked Jābir who was there; Jābir said “I,” and the Prophet repeated “I, I!” in apparent disapproval.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r7.anchor: روى الصحيحان وغيرهما عن جابر بن عبد الله

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r8.claim: The scholars explain that “I” does not identify the visitor; one should say one’s name, as Umar and Abū Mūsā did.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r8.anchor: إنما كره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك لأن قوله أنا لا يحصل بها تعريف

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r9.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r9.claim: Umar identified himself at the Prophet’s dwelling by greeting and asking whether Umar might enter; Muslim reports Abū Mūsā identifying himself to Umar as al-Ashʿarī.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#4/r9.anchor: ثبت عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في مشربة له

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r1.speaker: شعبة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r1.claim: When ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim answered “I” at Shuʿba’s door, Shuʿba joked that he had no friend named “I,” accompanying the report that the Prophet disliked that reply.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r1.anchor: منزل شعبة فدققت عليه الباب فقال: من هذا؟ قلت: أنا فقال: يا هذا ما لي صديق

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r2.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r2.claim: At ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd’s door, the answer “I” prompted him to reply that only God knows the unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r2.anchor: وذكر عن عمر بن شبة حدثنا محمد بن سلام عن أبيه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r3.speaker: علي بن المحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r3.claim: Al-Khaṭīb recounts ʿAlī ibn al-Muḥassin’s anecdote of a shaykh punning that “I” was the one who knocked.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r3.anchor: سمعت علي بن المحسن القاضي يحكي عن بعض الشيوخ

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r4.claim: Each community may use its customary local expression when seeking permission.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r4.anchor: ثم لكل قوم في الاستئذان عرفهم في العبارة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r5.claim: A report has Abū Hurayra at a door asking “andar?” and being answered “andarun,” a Persian permission expression.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r6.speaker: أحمد بن صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r6.claim: Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ says the Isfahani al-Darāwardī used “andarun” to invite entry in Medina, earning his nickname from it.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r6.anchor: أحمد بن صالح قال: كان الدراوردي من أهل أصبهان

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r7.speaker: كلدة بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r7.claim: Kalda ibn Ḥanbal entered the Prophet’s place in Mecca without greeting while delivering food from Ṣafwān ibn Umayya; the Prophet told him to return and greet, after Ṣafwān had become Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r7.anchor: روى أبو داود عن كلدة بن حنبل أن صفوان بن أمية بعثه

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r8.speaker: أبو الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r8.claim: Abū al-Zubayr reports from Jābir that the Prophet said not to admit someone who has not begun with the greeting.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r8.anchor: وروى أبو الزبير عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r9.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that ʿAṭāʾ heard Abū Hurayra instruct that someone asking to enter without greeting be told to bring the key; when ʿAṭāʾ supplied the greeting, Abū Hurayra agreed.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r9.anchor: أخبرني عطاء قال: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r10.speaker: حذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#5/r10.claim: When a man looked into Ḥudhayfa’s home before asking, Ḥudhayfa said he had already entered with his eye but not with his backside.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r1.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports that a messenger sent from one person to another constitutes permission; a related report says a meal invitation brought by a messenger also grants entry.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r1.anchor: أخرجه أبو داود أيضا عن أبي هريرة

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r2.claim: When eye contact occurs, the visitor owes the greeting, but being seen is not permission to enter; after greeting, ask and leave if refused.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r2.anchor: فإن وقعت العين على العين فالسلام قد تعين

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r3.claim: These rules concern other people’s homes; in one’s own home with family present, permission is unnecessary but one should greet them.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r3.anchor: هذه الأحكام كلها إنما هي في بيت ليس لك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r4.claim: Qatada says to greet the family when entering one’s own home, as they most deserve the greeting.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: إذا دخلت بيتك فسلم على أهلك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r5.claim: If one’s mother or sister is home, clear the throat or stamp one’s foot to alert them, since they may be in a state they would not want one to see.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r5.anchor: فإن كان فيه معك أمك أو أختك

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim reports Malik’s view that a man should seek permission before entering upon his mother or sister.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r6.anchor: قال ابن القاسم قال مالك: ويستأذن الرجل على أمه وأخته

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r7.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet told a man to seek permission to enter upon his mother even though he served her, asking if he would like to see her naked.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r8.claim: Scholars prescribe a formula invoking peace and blessed greetings when entering one’s empty home; the report via Ibn Wahb from the Prophet has a weak chain.

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r9.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r9.claim: Qatada says to greet oneself and God’s righteous servants in an empty home, and relates that angels answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: إذا دخلت بيتا ليس فيه أحد

QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:24:27#6/r10.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the sound position is to omit greeting and permission in an empty home; Qurtubi considers Qatada’s view good.
